body: Put constraints in a group with a marker interface, and pass the group to the validator to check only the constraints in it: public interface OnSignup {} @NotNull(groups = OnSignup.class) private String email; emailField.add(new PropertyValidator<>(OnSignup.class)); Constraints without a group belong to jakarta.validation.groups.Default; pass it as well when you want those checked too.

title: Best practices
text: The habits that keep a Wicket application easy to change and to test, each with the reason it follows from how Wicket works.
keywords: patterns anti-patterns guidelines conventions code style encapsulation onConfigure isVisible setVisible models serialization session factory wicket id naming refactoring Struts JSF
apis: Panel IModel LoadableDetachableModel Component WebSession IRequestCycleListener IComponentInstantiationListener
body: Developers who come to Wicket from request-based frameworks such as Struts or Spring MVC tend to write procedural code: build what this request needs, then throw it away. Wicket pages are long-lived objects in a tree, and code that treats them that way stays simpler. Each practice below follows from that.

title: Build the component tree once
text: Build the tree in the constructor or in onInitialize(), and then leave it alone. The tree is the skeleton; the models fill it with data. If you find yourself ca
body: Build the tree in the constructor or in onInitialize(), and then leave it alone. The tree is the skeleton; the models fill it with data. If you find yourself calling replace() or remove(), or adding different components depending on a condition, the data probably is not in a model. // Decided once, at construction: wrong after the user logs in if (MySession.get().isSignedIn()) { add(new EmptyPanel("login")); } else { add(new LoginPanel("login")); } Always add the LoginPanel, and let it decide when it is visible, as described in the next section.

title: Decide visibility in onConfigure
text: A component should decide for itself whether it is visible, based on current state. Set it in onConfigure(), which Wicket calls before every render: public clas
body: A component should decide for itself whether it is visible, based on current state. Set it in onConfigure(), which Wicket calls before every render: public class LoginPanel extends Panel { @Override protected void onConfigure() { super.onConfigure(); setVisible(!MySession.get().isSignedIn()); } } Calling setVisible() from outside, once, when you create the component, records a decision that goes stale: the page lives on, and something has to remember to call setVisible() again at the right moments. With onConfigure() the logic is in one place, inside the component it concerns, and it reads the current state on every render. The same goes for setEnabled(). When visibility depends on data, let the component read its model in onConfigure(); a button that shows something then only changes the model. Do not override isVisible() for this. Wicket calls it many times per request, also in phases where the answer must not change, and an override that depends on changing state leads to errors that are hard to trace. Form components inside an invisible or disabled container are not processed when the form is submitted.

title: Give a component its own markup
text: A component should hide how it is built. Whoever uses it should only need its constructor and its public methods, not the ids of its children. That rules out su
apis: Form WebMarkupContainer Every RegistrationForm Registration String IModel TextField LambdaModel Panel
body: A component should hide how it is built. Whoever uses it should only need its constructor and its public methods, not the ids of its children. That rules out subclassing Form or WebMarkupContainer and adding children to it: those classes have no markup of their own, so the page that uses the subclass has to supply tags for children it never added. // Every page that uses this form must know it has "username" and "email" fields public class RegistrationForm extends Form<Registration> { public RegistrationForm(String id, IModel<Registration> model) { super(id, model); add(new TextField<>("username", LambdaModel.of(model, Registration::getUsername, Registration::setUsername))); add(new TextField<>("email", LambdaModel.of(model, Registration::getEmail, Registration::setEmail))); } } Make it a Panel instead, with the form and the fields in the panel’s own markup. The page then contains one tag for the panel and nothing about its inside, and you can change the fields without touching any page. Adding behaviors and validators through a subclass is fine: they have no tags.

title: Keep classes and methods small
text: A page whose constructor builds everything in nested anonymous classes is hard to read and harder to change. Extract methods named after what they create, such
body: A page whose constructor builds everything in nested anonymous classes is hard to read and harder to change. Extract methods named after what they create, such as createAddressFields(), so the constructor reads as a summary of the page. When a part grows, make it a panel of its own. Smaller components are easier to reuse and to test.

title: Keep data in fields
text: A page is not recreated for every request. When a form fails validation, when the user clicks a link on the page, or when they come back with the back button, W
body: A page is not recreated for every request. When a form fails validation, when the user clicks a link on the page, or when they come back with the back button, Wicket uses the same page object. Data the page needs, which is usually a model passed to its constructor, belongs in a field, where every method of the page can reach it. Pages are stored by serializing them, so everything in their fields must be serializable and should be small. A service or a database connection does not belong in a field. Large or persistent data belongs in a LoadableDetachableModel, which keeps only what it needs to load the data again.

title: Let validators only validate
text: A validator answers one question: is this input acceptable? It should not change the input, the model or anything else. Nobody reading the form expects a valida
body: A validator answers one question: is this input acceptable? It should not change the input, the model or anything else. Nobody reading the form expects a validator to correct a bank name or save data. That work belongs in onSubmit() of the form or of a button, which runs after all validators passed.

title: Name ids after what they mean
text: Name a wicket:id after its business meaning, birthDate, not after the technology, birthDateTextField. The Java code and the markup already show what kind of com
body: Name a wicket:id after its business meaning, birthDate, not after the technology, birthDateTextField. The Java code and the markup already show what kind of component it is. When you replace the text field with a date picker, a technical id has to change in both files, and a business id does not. A CompoundPropertyModel uses the id as the name of a property, so setBirthDateTextField() would be the result.

title: Pass models, not objects
text: Give components and your own constructors an IModel<Registration>, not a Registration. A component that holds the object itself cannot get a fresh one: after th
body: Give components and your own constructors an IModel<Registration>, not a Registration. A component that holds the object itself cannot get a fresh one: after the next request the page still shows the entity it loaded the first time, even if the database changed. With a model, where the object comes from is the model’s business. The same component works with a Model, a lambda or a LoadableDetachableModel that loads the entity from the database each request.

title: Pass the model to the superclass
text: When your component takes a model, pass it to super(id, model). Wicket detaches the models a component knows about at the end of every request; a model you only
body: When your component takes a model, pass it to super(id, model). Wicket detaches the models a component knows about at the end of every request; a model you only keep in a field of your own is not detached unless you do it in onDetach(). A LoadableDetachableModel that is not detached keeps its loaded object, and the object ends up in the stored page.

title: Stay inside Wicket instead of using servlet filters
text: Code that needs to run around each request, such as opening and closing a unit of work, fits in an IRequestCycleListener, registered with getRequestCycleListene
body: Code that needs to run around each request, such as opening and closing a unit of work, fits in an IRequestCycleListener, registered with getRequestCycleListeners().add(). It has hooks such as onBeginRequest, onEndRequest and onException, and runs with Wicket’s request cycle, session and page available. Data that lives as long as the visit belongs in your WebSession, not in attributes of the HttpSession. Access the servlet API directly only when you must, for example to read a cookie set by another application, and keep that code in one place.

title: Subclass instead of using factories
text: A factory method that builds and configures a component hides its class. Callers cannot override onConfigure() or other methods, and cannot subclass it. Write a
body: A factory method that builds and configures a component hides its class. Callers cannot override onConfigure() or other methods, and cannot subclass it. Write a class instead, such as a CmsLabel that extends Label, and create it with new. If the factory exists to give components their services, use injection: an IComponentInstantiationListener runs for every component that is constructed. SpringComponentInjector from wicket-spring is one, and fills fields annotated with @SpringBean. See Inject Spring beans.

title: Test every page and component
text: Every page and panel should have at least a test that renders it with WicketTester. It catches a wicket:id without a component and a component without a tag, an
body: Every page and panel should have at least a test that renders it with WicketTester. It catches a wicket:id without a component and a component without a tag, and it runs in a fraction of the time of starting a server. Tests of forms and Ajax behaviors with FormTester and executeAjaxEvent catch errors in your logic before a user does. The tutorial Test a page with WicketTester shows how.

title: Unwrap models only in event methods
text: Do not call getObject() in a constructor. The constructor runs once, but the page lives for many requests, so a value you read there is a copy that goes stale a
body: Do not call getObject() in a constructor. The constructor runs once, but the page lives for many requests, so a value you read there is a copy that goes stale and takes up space in the stored page. Read models where you need their value now: in onSubmit(), onClick(), onUpdate(), in onConfigure(), or in a lambda model that Wicket evaluates during rendering.

title: Use callbacks instead of passing pages
text: Do not pass a page or component to a constructor so the new page can return to it later: // The caller must create the page to return to before it is needed pub
apis: The SettingsPage IModel Settings WebPage Form Override In CallingPage
body: Do not pass a page or component to a constructor so the new page can return to it later: // The caller must create the page to return to before it is needed public SettingsPage(IModel<Settings> settings, WebPage backTo) Give the page a method that runs when its work is done, and let the caller override it: public class SettingsPage extends WebPage { public SettingsPage(IModel<Settings> settings) { Form<Settings> form = new Form<>("form", settings) { @Override protected void onSubmit() { onSaved(); } }; add(form); } protected void onSaved() { } } // In the calling page setResponsePage(new SettingsPage(settingsModel) { @Override protected void onSaved() { setResponsePage(CallingPage.this); } }); The caller decides what happens next at the moment it matters, can do more than navigate, such as show a message, and no page is created that may never be shown.

title: Use the session only for global data
text: Wicket’s session is your own subclass of WebSession, with typed fields. Put data there that nearly every page needs during the whole visit: the signed-in user a
body: Wicket’s session is your own subclass of WebSession, with typed fields. Put data there that nearly every page needs during the whole visit: the signed-in user and what that user may do. Data of one form or one flow of pages does not belong there. Pass it from page to page in the constructor, as a model. It then lives exactly as long as the pages that use it, and disappears when the user leaves the flow, without code to clean it up.

title: Link to a page
text: Navigate to another page with a Link that runs code on the server first, or with a BookmarkablePageLink that points straight at the page.
keywords: anchor a href navigation onClick setResponsePage menu current page link text setBody
body: Every link starts as an tag with a wicket:id in the markup. Which component you attach to it depends on whether the click has to run code on the server. HomePage.html All products

title: Disable the link to the current page
text: In a menu, the entry for the page the user is on should not be a link. setAutoEnable(true) disables a link when it points to the page it is rendered on; for a B
body: In a menu, the entry for the page the user is on should not be a link. setAutoEnable(true) disables a link when it points to the page it is rendered on; for a BookmarkablePageLink that means a page of the same class. add(new BookmarkablePageLink<Void>("menuProducts", ProductListPage.class) .setAutoEnable(true)); A disabled link on an <a> tag renders without its href, so the browser shows plain text. Use onConfigure with setEnabled(...) to disable a link for other reasons, as with any component; see Show, hide or disable a component.

title: Link straight to a page with BookmarkablePageLink
text: When the link only navigates, use a BookmarkablePageLink. It renders the URL of the target page into the href, so the browser goes straight to that page, and th
body: When the link only navigates, use a BookmarkablePageLink. It renders the URL of the target page into the href, so the browser goes straight to that page, and the user can open it in a new tab or bookmark it. HomePage.java add(new BookmarkablePageLink<Void>("products", ProductListPage.class)); Pass PageParameters as the third argument to link to a page that needs them: add(new BookmarkablePageLink<Void>("product", ProductPage.class, new PageParameters().add("id", product.getId()))); The target page needs a constructor without arguments or one that takes PageParameters; see Pass parameters to a page. A BookmarkablePageLink does not make its own page stateful, which matters on stateless pages.

title: Open the target in a popup window
text: setPopupSettings opens the target page in a new browser window with the size and features you choose: add(new BookmarkablePageLink<Void>("help", HelpPage.class)
body: setPopupSettings opens the target page in a new browser window with the size and features you choose: add(new BookmarkablePageLink<Void>("help", HelpPage.class) .setPopupSettings(new PopupSettings("help").setWidth(600).setHeight(400))); For links to other sites, use an ExternalLink. For links written in plain HTML, without Java code, see Turn plain links into page links with wicket:link.

title: Run code when the user clicks with Link
text: A Link is a click handler. Its href points back to the link itself; when the user clicks, Wicket calls onClick() on the server. After onClick(), Wicket renders
apis: Link Void Override CartPage ConfirmPage StatelessLink BookmarkablePageLink
body: A Link is a click handler. Its href points back to the link itself; when the user clicks, Wicket calls onClick() on the server. After onClick(), Wicket renders the current page again unless you set another response page. add(new Link<Void>("delete") { @Override public void onClick() { cart.remove(item); setResponsePage(CartPage.class); } }); setResponsePage takes a page class or a page instance: setResponsePage(CartPage.class) and setResponsePage(CartPage.class, parameters) make Wicket create a new instance of the page, through a redirect to the URL of that page. setResponsePage(new ConfirmPage(order)) renders the instance you created. Use it when the next page needs objects or models that do not fit in a URL. Why the response is a redirect, and when it is not, is explained in Redirects after a request. Because its URL points at a component of the current page, a Link makes the page stateful. On a page that must stay stateless, use a StatelessLink or a BookmarkablePageLink.

title: Set the text of a link from a model
text: The markup between the <a> tags is the default text. To replace it from Java, give the link a body model. Here userModel is an IModel<User>: add(new Bookmarkabl
body: The markup between the <a> tags is the default text. To replace it from Java, give the link a body model. Here userModel is an IModel<User>: add(new BookmarkablePageLink<Void>("profile", ProfilePage.class) .setBody(userModel.map(User::getDisplayName))); The body is escaped like any model value.

title: Build a reusable panel
text: Package a piece of user interface as a Panel, a Java class with its own HTML file, and use it on any page as often as you need.
keywords: wicket:panel custom component reusable component partial include widget fragment of page component with markup
body: Use a panel when a piece of a page, with its markup and its components, appears in more than one place, or when a page gets too big to read. A panel is a component with its own markup file. Pages contain panels, panels contain other panels, and each one only knows its own markup.

title: Extend a panel
text: A panel can extend another panel and its markup, as pages do. Put <wicket:child/> in the base panel’s markup inside <wicket:panel>, and the subclass’s markup in
body: A panel can extend another panel and its markup, as pages do. Put <wicket:child/> in the base panel’s markup inside <wicket:panel>, and the subclass’s markup in <wicket:extend>. See Markup inheritance. For a small block of markup that only one page needs, a fragment saves you the class and the file.

title: Give the panel its own CSS
text: Ship the panel’s styles with the panel, so every page that uses it gets them. Contribute a stylesheet from renderHead: @Override public void renderHead(IHeaderR
body: Ship the panel’s styles with the panel, so every page that uses it gets them. Contribute a stylesheet from renderHead: @Override public void renderHead(IHeaderResponse response) { super.renderHead(response); response.render(CssHeaderItem.forReference( new CssResourceReference(AddressPanel.class, "AddressPanel.css"))); } Wicket adds the stylesheet once, however many panels are on the page. For a few lines you can also put a <style> inside <wicket:head> in the panel’s markup file. See Add CSS and JavaScript to a page.

title: Reach components inside a panel
text: From outside, refer to a panel’s child by its path, the ids separated by colons: Component city = get("billing:city"); Prefer to give the panel a method or a co
body: From outside, refer to a panel’s child by its path, the ids separated by colons: Component city = get("billing:city"); Prefer to give the panel a method or a constructor argument for what callers need to change. A path couples the caller to the panel’s insides.

title: Use the panel in a page
text:
Give the panel a tag in the page and add it like any component: CustomerPage.html

Billing address

Shipping address<
apis: Billing Shipping IModel Customer LoadableDetachableModel AddressPanel
body:
Give the panel a tag in the page and add it like any component: CustomerPage.html

Billing address

Shipping address

CustomerPage.java IModel customer = LoadableDetachableModel.of(() -> customers.find(customerId)); add(new AddressPanel("billing", customer.map(Customer::getBillingAddress))); add(new AddressPanel("shipping", customer.map(Customer::getShippingAddress))); The panel’s markup replaces the content of its tag. The tag itself,
here, stays.

title: Write the panel class
text: Subclass GenericPanel when the panel shows one object, so the model is typed. Use Panel when it has no model of its own. Add the panel’s components in the const
apis: GenericPanel Panel AddressPanel Address String IModel Override Label
body: Subclass GenericPanel when the panel shows one object, so the model is typed. Use Panel when it has no model of its own. Add the panel’s components in the constructor, or in onInitialize when they need the page or the parent. AddressPanel.java package com.example.customer; public class AddressPanel extends GenericPanel<Address> { public AddressPanel(String id, IModel<Address> address) { super(id, address); } @Override protected void onInitialize() { super.onInitialize(); add(new Label("street", getModel().map(Address::getStreet))); add(new Label("city", getModel().map(Address::getCity))); add(new Label("country", getModel().map(Address::getCountry))); } } getModel().map(...) derives a model for each field, so the labels always show the current address. See Read and write data with lambda models.

title: Write the panel’s markup
text: Give the HTML file the same name as the class, next to it in the same package: com/example/customer/AddressPanel.html. Wicket uses only what is inside <wicket:p
body:
Give the HTML file the same name as the class, next to it in the same package: com/example/customer/AddressPanel.html. Wicket uses only what is inside . Use the rest of the file for a preview. AddressPanel.html
Main Street 1
Springfield
USA
With Maven, put the HTML file either in src/main/java next to the class, if your build copies non-Java files from there, or in the same package under src/main/resources.

title: Where Wicket looks for texts
text: The exact order in which Wicket searches resource bundles for a key, the file names it tries, and the settings that change the search.
keywords: resource bundle lookup properties file order message key not found MissingResourceException wicket-package.properties utf8.properties properties.xml component path key override text translation priority
apis: Localizer IStringResourceLoader ComponentStringResourceLoader PackageStringResourceLoader ClassStringResourceLoader ValidatorStringResourceLoader InitializerStringResourceLoader ResourceSettings PropertiesFactory Component ResourceModel StringResourceModel
body: Every text that Wicket looks up by key, through Component#getString, ResourceModel, StringResourceModel, <wicket:message>, feedback messages of validators and converters, or the null option of a choice, goes through the Localizer. The Localizer asks a chain of string resource loaders, and each loader searches a set of bundles. The first text found wins. Why the search runs in this order is explained in How Wicket localizes.

title: File formats
text: For each name, the PropertiesFactory tries these extensions in order and uses the first file that exists. Files with different extensions for the same name are
body: For each name, the PropertiesFactory tries these extensions in order and uses the first file that exists. Files with different extensions for the same name are not merged. Extension Format Encoding .properties java.util.Properties ISO 8859-1; other characters as \uXXXX escapes .utf8.properties java.util.Properties UTF-8 .properties.xml XML properties, DTD http://java.sun.com/dtd/properties.dtd as declared in the XML header getResourceSettings().getPropertiesFactory() returns the factory; its getPropertiesLoaders() list can be changed to add or remove formats. Files are found through the resource stream locator of the application, on the classpath by default, next to the class files. In development mode Wicket checks the files for changes every second and reloads them.

title: File names
text: For each class or package in the search, Wicket builds names from the path of the class, the variation, the style and the locale: <path>[_<variation>][_<style>]
body: For each class or package in the search, Wicket builds names from the path of the class, the variation, the style and the locale: <path>[_<variation>][_<style>][_<language>[_<COUNTRY>[_<variant>]]] It tries the combinations from the most specific to the plain path. For com.example.OrderPage with variation compact, style acme and locale de_CH: # Name 1 com/example/OrderPage_compact_acme_de_CH 2 com/example/OrderPage_compact_acme_de 3 com/example/OrderPage_compact_acme 4 com/example/OrderPage_acme_de_CH 5 com/example/OrderPage_acme_de 6 com/example/OrderPage_acme 7 com/example/OrderPage_compact_de_CH 8 com/example/OrderPage_compact_de 9 com/example/OrderPage_compact 10 com/example/OrderPage_de_CH 11 com/example/OrderPage_de 12 com/example/OrderPage Combinations with an empty part are skipped: without a variation, names 1 to 3 and 7 to 9 are not tried. A locale variant adds _de_CH_<variant> before _de_CH in each group. The script and extensions of a locale are not used. Unlike java.util.ResourceBundle, Wicket does not fall back to the default locale of the JVM. After the language comes the name without a locale.

title: Find out why a text is not found
text: Set the log level of org.apache.wicket.resource.loader to DEBUG to log each class and key a loader tries, and of org.apache.wicket.Localizer to log where a key
body: Set the log level of org.apache.wicket.resource.loader to DEBUG to log each class and key a loader tries, and of org.apache.wicket.Localizer to log where a key was found or that it was not.

title: Inputs of a lookup
text: Input Taken from key the caller component the component the text is for; may be null locale Component#getLocale(), which asks the parents and finally Session#ge
body: Input Taken from key the caller component the component the text is for; may be null locale Component#getLocale(), which asks the parents and finally Session#getLocale() style Session#getStyle() variation Component#getVariation(), which asks the parents; null for a page unless overridden

title: Order of components and keys
text: ComponentStringResourceLoader walks the component path from the page down to the component that asks. At each component it first tries the key prefixed with the
apis: ComponentStringResourceLoader OrderPage OrderSummaryPanel Label WebPage Page WebMarkupContainer MarkupContainer WebComponent Component ListView Localizer PackageStringResourceLoader ClassStringResourceLoader Application ValidatorStringResourceLoader InitializerStringResourceLoader
body: ComponentStringResourceLoader walks the component path from the page down to the component that asks. At each component it first tries the key prefixed with the path that is left below that component, with ids joined by dots, and then the plain key. For a key title asked by the label total inside the panel summary on OrderPage: Step Bundles of Key 1 OrderPage summary.total.title 2 OrderPage title 3 OrderSummaryPanel (id summary) total.title 4 OrderSummaryPanel title 5 Label (id total) title Rule   Bundles of a component the bundle of its class, then of each superclass. The walk stops after the first Wicket base class it meets: WebPage, Page, WebMarkupContainer, MarkupContainer, WebComponent or Component Repeater items the ids of the items of a repeater, such as the index of a ListView item, are left out of the prefix: rows.name, not rows.0.name Component not on a page the walk starts at the topmost parent. Localizer logs a warning, because the parents that will hold it later are not searched; this happens when getString is called in a constructor Component null this loader finds nothing PackageStringResourceLoader and ClassStringResourceLoader use the same steps and keys. Instead of the bundle of each component class they search: Loader Bundles for a class PackageStringResourceLoader wicket-package in the package of the class, then in each parent package up to the root, then the same for each superclass ClassStringResourceLoader always the application class, then its superclasses up to and including org.apache.wicket.Application, whose bundle holds Wicket’s default messages ValidatorStringResourceLoader and InitializerStringResourceLoader try only the plain key, in the bundles of the validator or initializer class and its superclasses.

title: Settings
text: Setting Default Effect ResourceSettings#getStringResourceLoaders() the five loaders above the chain; a modifiable list ResourceSettings#setThrowExceptionOnMissi
apis: ResourceSettings MissingResourceException WicketRuntimeException Warning Property Localizer PackageStringResourceLoader String
body: Setting Default Effect ResourceSettings#getStringResourceLoaders() the five loaders above the chain; a modifiable list ResourceSettings#setThrowExceptionOnMissingResource(boolean) true when no text and no default is found, getString throws a MissingResourceException and <wicket:message> a WicketRuntimeException. With false, getString returns [Warning: Property for 'key' not found], and <wicket:message> logs a warning and renders its own body ResourceSettings#setUseDefaultOnMissingResource(boolean) true use the default text passed by the caller when the key is not found Localizer#setEnableCache(boolean) true cache results, including keys that were not found; clearCache() empties it PackageStringResourceLoader#setFilename(String) wicket-package base name of package bundles

title: String resource loaders
text: The default chain in ResourceSettings#getStringResourceLoaders(), asked in this order: # Loader Searches 1 ComponentStringResourceLoader bundles of the componen
apis: ResourceSettings ComponentStringResourceLoader PackageStringResourceLoader ClassStringResourceLoader Application ValidatorStringResourceLoader InitializerStringResourceLoader IInitializer BundleStringResourceLoader ResourceBundle NestedStringResourceLoader
body: The default chain in ResourceSettings#getStringResourceLoaders(), asked in this order: # Loader Searches 1 ComponentStringResourceLoader bundles of the components from the page down to the component, and of their superclasses 2 PackageStringResourceLoader wicket-package bundles in the packages of those components, up to the root package 3 ClassStringResourceLoader bundles of the application class and its superclasses, down to Wicket’s Application 4 ValidatorStringResourceLoader bundles of the validators of the form component, or the form validators of the form, that asks 5 InitializerStringResourceLoader bundles of the IInitializer classes of Wicket modules Two more loaders exist but are not in the default chain: BundleStringResourceLoader, which reads a Java ResourceBundle by base name, and NestedStringResourceLoader, which resolves references to other keys. See Load texts from your own source.

title: Inject CDI beans
text: Configure wicket-cdi so pages, components, behaviors and the session get CDI beans with @Inject, and choose beans that survive serialization.
keywords: Jakarta CDI contexts and dependency injection Weld Inject BeanManager Jakarta EE ApplicationScoped SessionScoped ConversationScoped passivation capable Tomcat Jetty beans.xml
body: Use this when your application runs with a CDI container, on a Jakarta EE server or on a servlet container with Weld, and your pages need CDI beans. Module wicket-cdi injects every component, behavior and session that Wicket creates, so fields annotated with @Inject work as they do in CDI beans. Wicket 10 is built against CDI 4.0 and tested with Weld 5.

title: Add wicket-cdi
text: <dependency> <groupId>org.apache.wicket</groupId> <artifactId>wicket-cdi</artifactId> <version>${wicket.version}</version> </dependency> A Jakarta EE server pro
body: <dependency> <groupId>org.apache.wicket</groupId> <artifactId>wicket-cdi</artifactId> <version>${wicket.version}</version> </dependency> A Jakarta EE server provides the CDI container. On Tomcat or Jetty, add Weld and start it with its servlet listener in web.xml: <dependency> <groupId>org.jboss.weld.servlet</groupId> <artifactId>weld-servlet-core</artifactId> <version>${weld.version}</version> </dependency> <listener> <listener-class>org.jboss.weld.environment.servlet.Listener</listener-class> </listener> Mark the jar or war with your beans as a bean archive with a beans.xml in META-INF (or WEB-INF for a war): <beans xmlns="https://jakarta.ee/xml/ns/jakartaee" version="4.0" bean-discovery-mode="annotated" />

title: Configure the application
text: Call CdiConfiguration.configure() in init(): WicketApplication.java @Override protected void init() { super.init(); new CdiConfiguration().configure(this); } Fr
body: Call CdiConfiguration.configure() in init(): WicketApplication.java @Override protected void init() { super.init(); new CdiConfiguration().configure(this); } From then on Wicket injects the application itself, every session, every component and every behavior when it is created.

title: Find the BeanManager
text: wicket-cdi looks up the BeanManager in JNDI under java:comp/BeanManager, then under java:comp/env/BeanManager, then through CDI.current(). When none of these wo
body: wicket-cdi looks up the BeanManager in JNDI under java:comp/BeanManager, then under java:comp/env/BeanManager, then through CDI.current(). When none of these work in your environment, pass it in: new CdiConfiguration() .setBeanManager(beanManager) .configure(this); setFallbackBeanManager() sets one that is used only when every lookup fails.

title: Inject a bean
text: Use @Inject, with qualifiers if you need them: @ApplicationScoped public class ProductService { public Product find(long id) { /* ... */ } } public class Produc
apis: Inject ApplicationScoped ProductService Product ProductPage WebPage PageParameters Label Component NonContextual ProductModel
body: Use @Inject, with qualifiers if you need them: @ApplicationScoped public class ProductService { public Product find(long id) { /* ... */ } } public class ProductPage extends WebPage { @Inject private ProductService products; public ProductPage(PageParameters parameters) { super(parameters); long id = parameters.get("id").toLong(); add(new Label("name", () -> products.find(id).getName())); } } The field is filled in the Component constructor, so you can use it in the constructor of your page. To inject an object that Wicket does not create, such as a model, use NonContextual: public ProductModel(long id) { this.id = id; NonContextual.of(this).inject(this); }

title: Inject only beans that survive serialization
text: Wicket serializes pages, and with them the injected fields. wicket-cdi does not wrap beans in proxies of its own, as the Spring and Guice integrations do. It re
apis: ApplicationScoped SessionScoped ConversationScoped RequestScoped Dependent Resource PersistenceContext PersistenceUnit WebServiceRef BeanManager Instance Event
body: Wicket serializes pages, and with them the injected fields. wicket-cdi does not wrap beans in proxies of its own, as the Spring and Guice integrations do. It relies on CDI, which guarantees serializable references only for passivation capable beans: beans with a normal scope (@ApplicationScoped, @SessionScoped, @ConversationScoped, @RequestScoped): CDI injects a serializable client proxy that finds the bean again after deserialization; @Dependent beans that are themselves serializable; stateless and singleton session beans; resources declared through a producer field with @Resource, @EJB, @PersistenceContext, @PersistenceUnit or @WebServiceRef; built-in beans such as BeanManager, Instance and Event. Give services a normal scope, usually @ApplicationScoped. The container also fills fields annotated with @EJB, @PersistenceContext or @Resource directly, but those references are not guaranteed to be serializable. For anything else, make the field transient or keep it out of the component. wicket-cdi does not inject a component again after it is deserialized, so a transient field is null when the page comes back from the page store, and the component may only use it during the request in which it was constructed.

title: Keep a conversation across pages
text: wicket-cdi propagates the CDI conversation from page to page. The ConversationPropagation mode decides when: Mode The conversation follows NONBOOKMARKABLE (defa
body: wicket-cdi propagates the CDI conversation from page to page. The ConversationPropagation mode decides when: Mode The conversation follows NONBOOKMARKABLE (default) Links and redirects to page instances, such as setResponsePage(new NextPage()). ALL Those and links to bookmarkable pages. NONE Nothing; turn propagation off. new CdiConfiguration() .setPropagation(ConversationPropagation.ALL) .configure(this); Start a long-running conversation with conversation.begin() on an injected Conversation. To let Wicket begin and end it for you, let a component on the page implement the marker interface ConversationalComponent: Wicket begins the conversation when such a page renders and ends it when the user reaches a page without one.

title: Chain models
text: Wrap one model in another so that a form, a panel or a label always works on the object the inner model currently holds.
keywords: nested model wrap model master-detail list detail selected item model pipeline dropdown selection
apis: ChainingModel CompoundPropertyModel LambdaModel FormComponentUpdatingBehavior PropertyModel IModel
body: Chain models when one component must work on whatever object another model holds at the moment, such as a form that edits the item selected in a drop-down. The outer model asks the inner model for its object every time, so it follows changes without being replaced. Most models in Wicket accept a model where they accept an object: CompoundPropertyModel, PropertyModel and LambdaModel.of(target, getter, setter). The models made with map, filter and the other default methods of IModel are chained to the model you call them on. Detaching the outer model detaches the inner one.

title: Chain a single property

title: Edit the item selected in a drop-down
text: This page shows a list of people in a drop-down and a form to edit the selected person. The drop-down and the form share one model, selected. The form wraps it
apis: CompoundPropertyModel Name Surname Email Save PersonListDetails WebPage IModel Person Model DropDownChoice LambdaChoiceRenderer FormComponentUpdatingBehavior Form Override TextField EmailTextField Serializable AjaxFormComponentUpdatingBehavior AjaxRequestTarget
body: This page shows a list of people in a drop-down and a form to edit the selected person. The drop-down and the form share one model, selected. The form wraps it in a CompoundPropertyModel, so its fields edit whichever person selected holds. PersonListDetails.html <select wicket:id="persons"></select> <form wicket:id="form"> <label>Name <input type="text" wicket:id="name"></label> <label>Surname <input type="text" wicket:id="surname"></label> <label>Email <input type="email" wicket:id="email"></label> <button type="submit">Save</button> </form> PersonListDetails.java public class PersonListDetails extends WebPage { public PersonListDetails() { IModel<Person> selected = Model.of(); DropDownChoice<Person> persons = new DropDownChoice<>("persons", selected, loadPersons(), new LambdaChoiceRenderer<>(Person::getFullName)); persons.add(new FormComponentUpdatingBehavior()); add(persons); Form<Person> form = new Form<>("form", new CompoundPropertyModel<>(selected)) { @Override protected void onConfigure() { super.onConfigure(); setVisible(getModelObject() != null); } }; form.add(new TextField<>("name")); form.add(new TextField<>("surname")); form.add(new EmailTextField("email")); add(form); } } loadPersons() returns the list of people to choose from. What happens: The user picks a person. FormComponentUpdatingBehavior submits the drop-down on its change event, without needing a form around it, and the drop-down writes the choice into selected. The page renders again. The form’s CompoundPropertyModel calls selected.getObject() and gets the new person. Each field reads its property from that person. The user edits the fields and saves. The fields write into the person that selected holds. The form never gets a new model. Only the object at the end of the chain changes. Person is Serializable here, so Model can hold it. When the people come from a database, hold the selection in a detachable model that keeps the id. To update only the form and not the whole page, use an AjaxFormComponentUpdatingBehavior and add the form to the AjaxRequestTarget, as in Update components with Ajax.

body: Extend ChainingModel for a custom model that may receive either an object or a model. When it was given a model, getObject() and setObject() go to that model; otherwise they read and replace the object itself. Its detach() detaches the inner model. getChainedModel() returns the inner model, or null when it was given a plain object. public class UpperCaseModel extends ChainingModel<String> { public UpperCaseModel(IModel<String> source) { super(source); } @Override public String getObject() { String value = super.getObject(); return value == null ? null : value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT); } } For a read-only transformation like this one, source.map(s -> s.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT)) is shorter. A subclass of ChainingModel pays off when it also writes, or when it is reused in many places.

body: The table lists every hook of Component in the order Wicket calls it during a request that renders a page. “Super” says where an override must call the super implementation. Wicket checks the ones marked “checked” and throws an IllegalStateException when the call is missing, with a message like onInitialize() in the hierarchy of com.example.HomePage has not called super.onInitialize(). Method Called by When Super Typical use constructor your code, or the page factory for bookmarkable pages once first line, by Java Add child components, set models. onInitialize() MarkupContainer.add() on a page that is already initialized; otherwise the page when it initializes itself before its first render once, parents before children first, checked Code that needs the page, the parent or the markup, such as getPage() or getMarkup(). onReAdd() MarkupContainer.add() each time a removed component is added again checked Restore what onRemove() released. onConfigure() Component.configure(), from the parent’s beforeRender() once per request, before rendering, also when the component is invisible checked Decide visibility and enabled state with setVisible() and setEnabled(). onBeforeRender() Component.beforeRender() once per request, after onConfigure(), only when visible last, checked Add, replace or remove children. The super call cascades to the children, so changes must come before it. renderHead(IHeaderResponse) the page’s <head> section, or the Ajax response for the updated components when the head is rendered, children before their parents not needed Contribute CSS and JavaScript. See Header items. onRender() Component.render() when the component renders depends on the class Writes the component to the response. Abstract; rarely overridden. onComponentTag(ComponentTag) onRender() of WebComponent and MarkupContainer while writing the component’s open tag yes, usually first Change the tag name or its attributes. onComponentTagBody(MarkupStream, ComponentTag) the component’s markup sourcing strategy after the open tag, for tags with a body call it to keep the default body Replace the body, for example with replaceComponentTagBody(). In a MarkupContainer, the super call renders the children. onAfterRender() Component.render() after the component and all its children are rendered, also when rendering threw an exception checked Clean up after rendering. onRemove() MarkupContainer.remove() and replace() when removed from the hierarchy, before its children last, checked Release resources held for rendering. onDetach() Component.detach() at the end of every request that used the page, also for components that did not render last, checked Release request-scoped state. detachModels() Component.detach(), after onDetach() at the end of every request yes Detach models other than the default model. body: A behavior is called from the matching hook of the component it is added to: Behavior method Called bind(Component) When the behavior is added to the component. onConfigure(Component) Right after the component’s onConfigure(). beforeRender(Component) Just before the component’s onRender(). renderHead(Component, IHeaderResponse) With the component’s renderHead(), when the behavior is enabled. onComponentTag(Component, ComponentTag) After the component’s onComponentTag(), when the open tag is written. afterRender(Component) Right after the component’s onRender(). onException(Component, RuntimeException) When rendering the component throws. onEvent(Component, IEvent<?>) After the component’s onEvent(). onRemove(Component) When the component is removed from the hierarchy. detach(Component) When the component detaches. unbind(Component) When the behavior is removed from the component.

title: Order within the component tree
text: onInitialize() runs on a container before its children. onConfigure() and onBeforeRender() run on a container before its children, because super.onBeforeRender(
body: onInitialize() runs on a container before its children. onConfigure() and onBeforeRender() run on a container before its children, because super.onBeforeRender() cascades to the children. Feedback components such as FeedbackPanel are prepared after all other components of the page, so they see the messages that onConfigure() and onBeforeRender() of other components report. renderHead() runs child first: children contribute before their parents, and the page contributes last, so a parent can override what a child contributed. onComponentTag() and onComponentTagBody() run in markup order. A container writes its open tag, then renders its children inside onComponentTagBody(), then writes its close tag. onAfterRender() runs on the children before their container. onDetach() runs on a container before its children. Once rendering has started, a component cannot change: adding or replacing children throws an exception. Make such changes in onBeforeRender() before calling super, or in onConfigure().

title: Stages
text: Stage When Hook methods Construction Application code calls new; for bookmarkable pages Wicket calls the page constructor. Once per component. constructor Initi
body: Stage When Hook methods Construction Application code calls new; for bookmarkable pages Wicket calls the page constructor. Once per component. constructor Initialization The first time the component is part of a tree rooted in a page. Once per component. onInitialize() Re-adding The component was removed from its parent and is added to a page again. onReAdd() Configuration Every request in which the component, or a container around it, is about to render. onConfigure() Preparing to render Every request in which the component will render and is visible. onBeforeRender() Rendering The component writes its markup. Happens for a full page render and for an Ajax update of the component or a parent. renderHead(), onRender(), onComponentTag(), onComponentTagBody(), onAfterRender() Removal The parent calls remove() or replace(). Optional, and never happens to a page. onRemove() Detaching The end of every request in which the component’s page was used. onDetach(), detachModels() A component that is not visible goes through configuration but not through preparing to render or rendering.

title: When a request invokes a listener

body: When the request clicks a link or submits a form, Wicket loads the page and calls the listener (onClick(), onSubmit(), the onEvent() of an Ajax behavior) before any of the rendering hooks of that request. The listener sees the visibility and enabled state set during the previous render. After the listener, the page or the updated components go through configuration and rendering as above, and every touched component is detached at the end.

title: Compress responses with gzip

body: Wicket does not gzip or brotli-compress responses itself. Turn on response compression in the servlet container or in the reverse proxy in front of it; it applies to pages and resources alike.

page: Minify and compress CSS and JavaScript
title: Plug in a compressor
text: A compressor is an object with one method, compress(String), that returns the new content. Set one for CSS and one for JavaScript: @Override protected void init
apis: String Override MyCssMinifier MyJsMinifier CompositeCssCompressor CompositeJavaScriptCompressor CssUrlReplacer NoOpTextCompressor
body: A compressor is an object with one method, compress(String), that returns the new content. Set one for CSS and one for JavaScript: @Override protected void init() { super.init(); if (usesDeploymentConfig()) { getResourceSettings().setCssCompressor(css -> MyCssMinifier.minify(css)); getResourceSettings().setJavaScriptCompressor(js -> MyJsMinifier.minify(js)); } } There is no CSS compressor by default. To run several compressors in turn, combine them with CompositeCssCompressor or CompositeJavaScriptCompressor: getResourceSettings().setCssCompressor( new CompositeCssCompressor(new CssUrlReplacer(), css -> MyCssMinifier.minify(css))); Wicket runs the compressor each time it sends the file, so keep it fast; browsers keep the result for as long as the version in the URL stays the same. A reference with readBuffered(false) is streamed and skips the compressor. Setting null, or new NoOpTextCompressor(), switches compression off.

page: Minify and compress CSS and JavaScript
title: Rewrite URLs inside stylesheets
text: CssUrlReplacer is a CSS compressor that does not compress. It finds the relative url(…) references in a stylesheet and replaces them with Wicket URLs for the pa
body: CssUrlReplacer is a CSS compressor that does not compress. It finds the relative url(…) references in a stylesheet and replaces them with Wicket URLs for the package resources they point to, including the version, so images referenced from CSS are cached as long as the CSS itself: getResourceSettings().setCssCompressor(new CssUrlReplacer()); With mycss.css in com/example/res/css/ and an image in com/example/res/images/, this rule body { background-image: url('../images/some.png'); } is served as body { background-image: url('../images/some-ver-1712345678000.png'); } Absolute URLs, context-relative URLs that start with / and data: URLs stay as they are. Pass file names to the constructor, new CssUrlReplacer(List.of("vendor.css")), to leave those stylesheets alone. Add ?embedBase64 to a URL to embed the image in the stylesheet as a data: URL: .logo { background-image: url('../images/logo.png?embedBase64'); } The default Content Security Policy blocks images from data: URLs. Allow them with getCspSettings().blocking().add(CSPDirective.IMG_SRC, "data:"), see Configure the Content Security Policy.

title: Ship minified files
text: Put the minified version next to the original, with .min before the extension: com/example/components/ calendar.js calendar.min.js calendar.css calendar.min.css
body: Put the minified version next to the original, with .min before the extension: com/example/components/ calendar.js calendar.min.js calendar.css calendar.min.css Keep referencing calendar.js. When minified resources are in use, Wicket serves calendar.min.js if it exists and falls back to calendar.js otherwise. Minified resources are off in development mode, so you debug the readable files, and on in deployment mode. To change that, set it in init(): getResourceSettings().setUseMinifiedResources(false); Files in the web application folder follow the same naming rule with ContextRelativeResourceReference, but without the fallback, see Use files from the web application root. Whether the compressors described below run depends on the name you reference: a reference to calendar.min.js is never compressed, but when Wicket picks calendar.min.js for a reference to calendar.js, the compressor runs on the minified file as well.

body: A Wicket application is a Jakarta web application. The servlet container starts a WicketFilter, which creates the application object, calls its initialization, and then handles every request mapped to the filter. WicketServlet does the same as a servlet, for containers or setups where a filter does not fit. web.xml <filter> <filter-name>wicket.myproject</filter-name> <filter-class>org.apache.wicket.protocol.http.WicketFilter</filter-class> <init-param> <param-name>applicationClassName</param-name> <param-value>com.mycompany.WicketApplication</param-value> </init-param> </filter> <filter-mapping> <filter-name>wicket.myproject</filter-name> <url-pattern>/*</url-pattern> </filter-mapping> Without web.xml, annotate a subclass of WicketFilter: ProjectFilter.java @WebFilter(value = "/*", initParams = { @WebInitParam(name = "applicationClassName", value = "com.mycompany.WicketApplication"), @WebInitParam(name = "filterMappingUrlPattern", value = "/*") }) public class ProjectFilter extends WicketFilter { } Filter parameters Parameter Meaning applicationClassName Fully qualified name of your WebApplication subclass. Read by the default application factory, ContextParamWebApplicationFactory. applicationFactoryClassName An IWebApplicationFactory that creates the application instead, such as org.apache.wicket.spring.SpringWebApplicationFactory to take the application from a Spring context. applicationBean With SpringWebApplicationFactory: the name of the application bean, if the context has more than one. filterMappingUrlPattern The URL pattern the filter is mapped to, such as /* or /app/*. Wicket reads it from this parameter first, then from web.xml, then from a @WebFilter annotation on the filter class. ignorePaths Comma-separated paths the filter passes on to the rest of the filter chain, such as /static,/health. configuration, wicket.configuration development or deployment. Also read as a context parameter. See Runtime configuration type. sourceFolder Development mode only: an extra folder in which Wicket looks for markup and resources. Initialization order When the filter starts, Application.initApplication() runs these steps: Step What happens internalInit() Wicket’s own defaults: error pages, resource finders, component resolvers, the settings for the runtime configuration type, and the strict content security policy. Initializers The IInitializer implementations listed in META-INF/services/org.apache.wicket.IInitializer of the jars on the classpath, such as the one of wicket-jmx. See Configure a module with an initializer. init() Your configuration. Application listeners IApplicationListener.onAfterInitialized. validateInit() Checks the configuration and installs the content security policy and the COOP and COEP listeners. Your init() runs after Wicket’s defaults, so a setting you change there sticks.
