The tables list the main options; see the Javadoc of each class for all of them. ApplicationSettings getApplicationSettings(): error pages, uploads and class loading. Setting Default Meaning setPageExpiredErrorPage(Class) PageExpiredErrorPage Page shown when a requested page is no longer stored. setInternalErrorPage(Class) InternalErrorPage Page shown for an unexpected exception in deployment mode. setAccessDeniedPage(Class) AccessDeniedPage Page shown when authorization denies access. setDefaultMaximumUploadSize(Bytes) Bytes.MAX Largest upload a form accepts, unless the form sets its own. setUploadProgressUpdatesEnabled(boolean) false Track upload progress, needed for UploadProgressBar. setClassResolver(IClassResolver) DefaultClassResolver How Wicket loads classes by name, for example in OSGi. setFeedbackMessageCleanupFilter(IFeedbackMessageFilter) DefaultCleanupFeedbackMessageFilter Which feedback messages are removed at the end of a request. DebugSettings getDebugSettings(): checks and aids for development. Setting Default Meaning setComponentUseCheck(boolean) true (mode) Fail when a component added in Java has no tag in the markup. setAjaxDebugModeEnabled(boolean) false (mode) Load the Ajax debug window in the browser. setDevelopmentUtilitiesEnabled(boolean) false (mode) Allow the wicket-devutils components and pages. setOutputMarkupContainerClassName(boolean) false Write the class of each container as an HTML comment in the output. setComponentPathAttributeName(String) none Write each component’s path in an attribute of this name, for example for UI tests. setLinePreciseReportingOnAddComponentEnabled(boolean) false Record where components are added, for better error messages. Slow. “(mode)” marks a setting that the runtime configuration type overwrites, see Development and deployment defaults. ExceptionSettings getExceptionSettings(): what happens on unexpected exceptions. Setting Default Meaning setUnexpectedExceptionDisplay(UnexpectedExceptionDisplay) SHOW_EXCEPTION_PAGE (mode) SHOW_EXCEPTION_PAGE shows the stack trace, SHOW_INTERNAL_ERROR_PAGE the internal error page, SHOW_NO_EXCEPTION_PAGE only an HTTP 500. setAjaxErrorHandlingStrategy(AjaxErrorStrategy) REDIRECT_TO_ERROR_PAGE On an exception in an Ajax request, redirect to the error page, or INVOKE_FAILURE_HANDLER to let client-side failure handlers react. setThreadDumpStrategy(ThreadDumpStrategy) THREAD_HOLDING_LOCK Which stack traces to log when a request cannot get the lock on a page: NO_THREADS, THREAD_HOLDING_LOCK or ALL_THREADS. setNotRenderableErrorStrategy(NotRenderableErrorStrategy) LOG_WARNING What to do when a component that renders no tag of its own, because of setRenderBodyOnly(true) or a wicket: tag, is asked for a markup id or placeholder tag: LOG_WARNING or THROW_EXCEPTION. FrameworkSettings getFrameworkSettings(): framework-wide hooks. Setting Default Meaning getVersion()   The Wicket version, read from the jar. setSerializer(ISerializer) JavaSerializer How pages are serialized for the page store. setDetachListener(IDetachListener) none Called each time a component detaches. add(IEventDispatcher) none Extra dispatchers for Wicket events. JavaScriptLibrarySettings getJavaScriptLibrarySettings(): the JavaScript Wicket loads for Ajax. Setting Default Meaning setJQueryReference(ResourceReference) jQuery 3 The jQuery version Wicket loads. setWicketAjaxReference(ResourceReference) WicketAjaxJQueryResourceReference Wicket’s Ajax library. MarkupSettings getMarkupSettings(): how markup is read and written. Setting Default Meaning setStripWicketTags(boolean) false (mode) Remove wicket: tags and attributes from the output. setStripComments(boolean) false Remove HTML comments from the markup. setCompressWhitespace(boolean) false Collapse whitespace in the markup. setDefaultMarkupEncoding(String) none, the encoding of the operating system Encoding of markup files without an XML declaration. setAutomaticLinking(boolean) false Treat every page that contains links as if surrounded by wicket:link. setMarkupIdGenerator(IMarkupIdGenerator) DefaultMarkupIdGenerator How Wicket generates id attributes. PageSettings getPageSettings(): pages and their versions. Setting Default Meaning setVersionPagesByDefault(boolean) true Store a new version of a page when it changes, so the back button returns to the earlier state. setRecreateBookmarkablePagesAfterExpiry(boolean) true Create a new instance of a bookmarkable page instead of showing the page-expired error. setCallListenerAfterExpiry(boolean) false After recreating an expired page, still run the link or form callback that was requested. addComponentResolver(IComponentResolver)   Resolve tags in markup to components that are not added in Java. RequestCycleSettings getRequestCycleSettings(): how requests are handled and responses written. Setting Default Meaning setRenderStrategy(RenderStrategy) REDIRECT_TO_BUFFER Render after an action and redirect to the buffered result; REDIRECT_TO_RENDER and ONE_PASS_RENDER are the alternatives. See Redirects after a request. setResponseRequestEncoding(String) UTF-8 Encoding of requests and responses. setTimeout(Duration) 1 minute How long a request waits for an earlier request on the same page to finish. setBufferResponse(boolean) true Buffer the response, so headers can still change while rendering. setGatherExtendedBrowserInfo(boolean) false Collect browser details, such as the time zone, with an extra round trip. addResponseFilter(IResponseFilter)   Post-process the rendered response. setExceptionRetryCount(int) 10 How many times Wicket tries to render the error response for an exception before it gives up. RequestLoggerSettings getRequestLoggerSettings(): the request logger. Setting Default Meaning setRequestLoggerEnabled(boolean) false Log every request with its handler and session. setRequestsWindowSize(int) 0 Number of requests the logger keeps in memory. With 0 it only keeps totals per session. setRecordSessionSize(boolean) false Measure and log the session size. Costly. ResourceSettings getResourceSettings(): markup, resources and resource bundles. Setting Default Meaning setResourcePollFrequency(Duration) 1 second in development, none in deployment (mode) How often Wicket checks markup and resource files for changes. setUseMinifiedResources(boolean) true, false in development (mode) Serve .min.js and .min.css variants of package resources when they exist. setJavaScriptCompressor(IJavaScriptCompressor) none, DefaultJavaScriptCompressor in deployment (mode) Compress JavaScript package resources. setCssCompressor(ICssCompressor) none Compress CSS package resources. setCachingStrategy(IResourceCachingStrategy) version in file name How resource URLs carry a version so browsers can cache them: the last-modified time in development, a content digest in deployment. setDefaultCacheDuration(Duration) 365 days How long browsers may cache resources. setPackageResourceGuard(IPackageResourceGuard) SecurePackageResourceGuard Which files in Java packages may be served. getResourceFinders() web application root, META-INF/resources Where Wicket looks for markup and resources besides the classpath. getStringResourceLoaders()   Where Wicket looks for localized texts. setThrowExceptionOnMissingResource(boolean) true Fail when a text resource is missing. setUseDefaultOnMissingResource(boolean) true Use a default value, if one is given, when a text resource is missing. SecuritySettings getSecuritySettings(): authorization, encryption and isolation headers. Setting Default Meaning setAuthorizationStrategy(IAuthorizationStrategy) ALLOW_ALL Decides whether components may be created and rendered. setUnauthorizedComponentInstantiationListener(...) throws UnauthorizedInstantiationException Called when a component may not be created. setEnforceMounts(boolean) false Refuse requests for a mounted page through its generic bookmarkable URL instead of its mount path. setCryptFactory(ICryptFactory) key in session Creates the objects that encrypt URLs. setRandomSupplier(ISecureRandomSupplier) DefaultSecureRandomSupplier Source of secure random data. setCrossOriginOpenerPolicyConfiguration(...) SAME_ORIGIN The Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header. setCrossOriginEmbedderPolicyConfiguration(...) REPORTING The Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy header. StoreSettings getStoreSettings(): where pages are kept between requests. Setting Default Meaning setMaxSizePerSession(Bytes) 10 MB Disk space per session for stored pages. setFileStoreFolder(File) the container’s temporary folder Folder of the disk page store. setAsynchronous(boolean) true Write pages to disk on a background thread. setAsynchronousQueueCapacity(int) 100 Pages waiting to be written before writes become synchronous. setEncrypted(boolean) false Encrypt pages before they are written. setCrypter(Supplier<ICrypter>) DefaultCrypter The cipher for encrypted pages. Content security policy getCspSettings() on WebApplication returns the ContentSecurityPolicySettings. blocking() and reporting() return the configuration of the enforced and the report-only header, to which you add directives. Wicket sets a strict policy with a nonce for scripts and styles by default. See Configure the Content Security Policy. Listener collections Application also holds collections of listeners, each with an add method: Getter Listeners for getRequestCycleListeners() Start, end, exceptions and handlers of each request. getComponentInstantiationListeners() Every component constructor, used for dependency injection. getComponentInitializationListeners() onInitialize of every component. getComponentOnConfigureListeners() onConfigure of every component. getHeaderContributorListeners() Contributions to the <head> of every page. getSessionListeners() Creation and invalidation of sessions. getApplicationListeners() Initialization and destruction of the application.

title: Configure the page store
text: Change how much page history Wicket keeps per session and where, encrypt stored pages, or replace the disk store with another store.
keywords: page store size maxSizePerSession filestore folder disk space asynchronous encrypt pages crypt scheme Bouncy Castle GCM-SIV in-memory cluster session replication setPageManagerProvider serializer Kryo
apis: StoreSettings DefaultPageManagerProvider CryptingPageStore InMemoryPageStore InSessionPageStore FilePageStore SecuritySettings DebugBar
body: Configure the page store when the defaults do not fit: too little or too much page history per session, a temporary directory that is not suitable, stored pages that must be encrypted, or a cluster where pages must be reachable from every node. All settings go in your application’s init(). How pages are stored explains the stores involved.

title: Change the serializer
text: Pages are serialized with Java serialization. Plug in another ISerializer, for example a Kryo-based one from WicketStuff: getFrameworkSettings().setSerializer(n
body: Pages are serialized with Java serialization. Plug in another ISerializer, for example a Kryo-based one from WicketStuff: getFrameworkSettings().setSerializer(new MySerializer());

title: Check the size of pages and sessions
text: The DebugBar from wicket-devutils shows the size of the session while you develop, and links to an inspector of the current page and to a browser of the page st
body: The DebugBar from wicket-devutils shows the size of the session while you develop, and links to an inspector of the current page and to a browser of the page store. Add it to a base page: add(new DebugBar("debug"));

title: Encrypt stored pages
text: Turn on encryption when the stored pages hold data that others with access to the disk must not read: getStoreSettings().setEncrypted(true); Each session gets a
body: Turn on encryption when the stored pages hold data that others with access to the disk must not read: getStoreSettings().setEncrypted(true); Each session gets a random key, kept in the session. The cipher comes from StoreSettings.setCrypter. The default DefaultCrypter uses AES-256-CBC, which is not authenticated. For tamper detection, use the GCM-SIV crypter, which needs Bouncy Castle: getStoreSettings().setEncrypted(true).setCrypter(GCMSIVCrypter::new);

title: Limit the history per session
text: Each session’s pages go to a file of at most 10 MB. When it is full, the oldest pages are overwritten, and going back to them ends in an expired page. Raise the
body: Each session’s pages go to a file of at most 10 MB. When it is full, the oldest pages are overwritten, and going back to them ends in an expired page. Raise the limit for applications where users go back far, lower it to save disk: getStoreSettings().setMaxSizePerSession(Bytes.megabytes(20));

title: Move the store folder
text: By default the files go to the servlet container’s temporary directory, in a folder named after the application followed by -filestore. Choose a folder that onl
body: By default the files go to the servlet container’s temporary directory, in a folder named after the application followed by -filestore. Choose a folder that only the application can read, with enough space: getStoreSettings().setFileStoreFolder(new File("/var/lib/myapp/pages"));

title: Replace the disk store
text: Register a DefaultPageManagerProvider that creates another persistent store. The rest of the default chain stays as it is. Keep the pages in the application’s m
apis: DefaultPageManagerProvider Override IPageStore InMemoryPageStore Bytes InSessionPageStore StoreSettings FilePageStore SerializingPageStore SerializedPage
body: Register a DefaultPageManagerProvider that creates another persistent store. The rest of the default chain stays as it is. Keep the pages in the application’s memory, at most 50 per session: setPageManagerProvider(new DefaultPageManagerProvider(this) { @Override protected IPageStore newPersistentStore() { return new InMemoryPageStore(getName(), 50); } }); InMemoryPageStore also takes a Bytes limit instead of a page count. Its pages are lost when the server stops, and other nodes in a cluster cannot see them. Keep serialized pages in the HTTP session, up to 2 MB per session. The servlet container then replicates them with the session, which suits a cluster with session replication. The session cannot be written from a background thread, so switch off asynchronous writing as well: getStoreSettings().setAsynchronous(false); setPageManagerProvider(new DefaultPageManagerProvider(this) { @Override protected IPageStore newPersistentStore() { return new InSessionPageStore(Bytes.megabytes(2)); } }); Write each page to its own file instead of one file per session, which keeps pages from different browser tabs from pushing each other out: setPageManagerProvider(new DefaultPageManagerProvider(this) { @Override protected IPageStore newPersistentStore() { StoreSettings settings = getStoreSettings(); return new FilePageStore(getName(), settings.getFileStoreFolder(), settings.getMaxSizePerSession()); } }); DefaultPageManagerProvider has a factory method for each store in the chain, such as newCachingStore and newSerializingStore, to replace other parts. Stores for databases and distributed caches are available from WicketStuff, or implement IPageStore yourself. Any store after the SerializingPageStore receives SerializedPages.

title: Write pages synchronously
text: Pages are written to disk on a background thread, with a queue of 100 pages. Writes beyond that capacity happen in the request thread. Change the capacity, or w
body: Pages are written to disk on a background thread, with a queue of 100 pages. Writes beyond that capacity happen in the request thread. Change the capacity, or write every page in the request: getStoreSettings().setAsynchronousQueueCapacity(200); getStoreSettings().setAsynchronous(false);

page: Use files from the web application root
title: Use files from the web application root
text: Add stylesheets, scripts and images that live in the web application folder, such as src/main/webapp, to your pages with ContextRelativeResourceReference and ContextImage.
keywords: webapp folder src/main/webapp context root absolute path site.css theme min.js minified ServletContext resource
body: Use this when a file is not part of a component but belongs to the whole site, such as a theme stylesheet, a logo or a script that a design team delivers into the web application folder: src/main/webapp/ css/site.css css/site.min.css js/site.js img/logo.png

page: Use files from the web application root
title: Add a stylesheet or script from the web application folder
text: Create a ContextRelativeResourceReference with the path from the root of the web application, and render it as a header item, usually from a base page: BasePage
apis: ContextRelativeResourceReference BasePage WebPage Override IHeaderResponse CssHeaderItem JavaScriptHeaderItem
body: Create a ContextRelativeResourceReference with the path from the root of the web application, and render it as a header item, usually from a base page: BasePage.java public abstract class BasePage extends WebPage { private static final ContextRelativeResourceReference SITE_CSS = new ContextRelativeResourceReference("css/site.css"); private static final ContextRelativeResourceReference SITE_JS = new ContextRelativeResourceReference("js/site.js", false); @Override public void renderHead(IHeaderResponse response) { super.renderHead(response); response.render(CssHeaderItem.forReference(SITE_CSS)); response.render(JavaScriptHeaderItem.forReference(SITE_JS)); } } Wicket serves the file through its resource handling, so the URL contains a version that changes with the file, the response gets long cache headers, and the tag gets the Content Security Policy nonce. A plain <link href="/css/site.css"> or <script src="/js/site.js"> in the markup has no nonce, and the default Content Security Policy blocks it. See Configure the Content Security Policy.

page: Use files from the web application root
title: Link a file by URL without versioning
text: CssHeaderItem.forUrl and JavaScriptHeaderItem.forUrl write the URL you give them, with the nonce. A relative URL is resolved against the root of the web applica
body: CssHeaderItem.forUrl and JavaScriptHeaderItem.forUrl write the URL you give them, with the nonce. A relative URL is resolved against the root of the web application, not against the current page: response.render(CssHeaderItem.forUrl("css/print.css", "print")); The URL carries no version, so browsers may keep an old copy after a deployment. Use it for files that never change or that you version yourself.

page: Use files from the web application root
title: Serve the minified file in deployment mode
text: By default the reference switches to the minified file when the application uses minified resources, which is the case in deployment mode. In the example, css/s
body: By default the reference switches to the minified file when the application uses minified resources, which is the case in deployment mode. In the example, css/site.css becomes css/site.min.css. The reference does not fall back to the original name: when you use the default constructor, the .min file must exist next to every file you reference. Choose per file: Constructor Development mode Deployment mode new ContextRelativeResourceReference("css/site.css") css/site.css css/site.min.css new ContextRelativeResourceReference("js/site.js", false) js/site.js js/site.js new ContextRelativeResourceReference("js/site.js", "minified") js/site.js js/site.minified.js Whether minified files are used follows getResourceSettings().setUseMinifiedResources(…); Minify and compress CSS and JavaScript describes that setting.

page: Use files from the web application root
title: Show an image from the web application folder
text: ContextImage renders an whose src is a path from the root of the web application: BasePage.java add(new ContextImage("logo", "img/logo.png")); BasePage.ht
body: ContextImage renders an whose src is a path from the root of the web application: BasePage.java add(new ContextImage("logo", "img/logo.png")); BasePage.html The path can also come from a model, new ContextImage("logo", logoPathModel), to switch images per tenant or theme. For files that belong to a component, prefer package resources: Serve files from your Java packages.

title: Convert input to your types
text: Tell a field which type its input becomes, write a converter for your own type and register it for one field or the whole application.
keywords: converter type conversion setType not a valid parse format newConverterLocator createConverter
apis: IConverter ConverterLocator IConverterLocator ConversionException FormComponent String
body: You need this when a field holds something other than a String and the default conversion does not do what you want, or does not know your type. Conversion runs after the required check and before the validators; How a form is processed explains why.

title: Change the conversion error message
text: A failed conversion reports the message with key IConverter: “The value of ‘${label}’ is not a valid ${type}.” Wicket first tries IConverter.<Type>, so you can
apis: IConverter Type ConversionException YearMonthConverter Enter Integer
body: A failed conversion reports the message with key IConverter: “The value of ‘${label}’ is not a valid ${type}.” Wicket first tries IConverter.<Type>, so you can word it per type. A resource key set on the ConversionException is tried before both. Put the keys in a properties file of the page or application: WicketApplication.properties YearMonthConverter=Enter ${label} as ${format}, for example 03/2027. IConverter.Integer=${label} must be a whole number. Variables you set on the exception, such as ${format} above, are available in the message, next to ${label}, ${input} and ${type}.

title: Choices convert differently
text: DropDownChoice, RadioChoice and the other choice components do not use converters. They map the submitted option id back to one of their choices with their ICho
body: DropDownChoice, RadioChoice and the other choice components do not use converters. They map the submitted option id back to one of their choices with their IChoiceRenderer. See Let the user pick from a list.

title: Register the converter for the whole application
text: Override newConverterLocator() in your application. Start from a ConverterLocator, which already holds the default converters, and add yours: WicketApplication.
apis: ConverterLocator Override IConverterLocator YearMonth YearMonthConverter Label
body: Override newConverterLocator() in your application. Start from a ConverterLocator, which already holds the default converters, and add yours: WicketApplication.java @Override protected IConverterLocator newConverterLocator() { ConverterLocator locator = new ConverterLocator(); locator.set(YearMonth.class, new YearMonthConverter()); return locator; } Every component whose type is YearMonth now uses it, both for input and for display. A Label with a YearMonth model renders as 03/2027 too.

title: Tell the field its type
text: A field converts its input to its type. It finds the type in this order: The type you pass to the constructor or set with setType(Class). The object class repor
apis: Class PropertyModel CompoundPropertyModel Model String TextField Integer LambdaModel Order Boolean Character BigDecimal BigInteger Date Calendar LocalDate LocalDateTime LocalTime ZonedDateTime
body: A field converts its input to its type. It finds the type in this order: The type you pass to the constructor or set with setType(Class). The object class reported by the model. PropertyModel and CompoundPropertyModel know the type of their property; Model knows the class of its current object, if it has one. Otherwise the input stays a String. Lambda models do not report a type, so pass it yourself: TextField<Integer> quantity = new TextField<>("quantity", LambdaModel.of(order, Order::getQuantity, Order::setQuantity), Integer.class); Without Integer.class, Wicket would try to put a String into an Integer property. Setting a primitive type such as int.class also makes the field required. Wicket converts the common types out of the box: numbers, Boolean, Character, BigDecimal, BigInteger, java.util.Date, Calendar, the java.sql date types, LocalDate, LocalDateTime, LocalTime and ZonedDateTime. Validators and converters lists them with their formats.

title: Use a converter for one field
text: Override createConverter on the component. Return null for types you do not handle, so the application’s converters still apply. TextField<YearMonth> expiry = n
apis: TextField YearMonth LambdaModel Card Override IConverter Class YearMonthConverter
body: Override createConverter on the component. Return null for types you do not handle, so the application’s converters still apply. TextField<YearMonth> expiry = new TextField<>("expiry", LambdaModel.of(card, Card::getExpiry, Card::setExpiry), YearMonth.class) { @Override protected IConverter<?> createConverter(Class<?> type) { return YearMonth.class.equals(type) ? new YearMonthConverter() : null; } };

title: Write a converter
text: Implement IConverter with both directions: from the input string to your object, and from your object to the string shown in the field. Throw a ConversionExcept
apis: IConverter ConversionException YearMonthConverter YearMonth DateTimeFormatter Override String Locale DateTimeParseException
body: Implement IConverter with both directions: from the input string to your object, and from your object to the string shown in the field. Throw a ConversionException when the input cannot be read. YearMonthConverter.java public class YearMonthConverter implements IConverter<YearMonth> { private static final DateTimeFormatter FORMAT = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("MM/yyyy"); @Override public YearMonth convertToObject(String value, Locale locale) { try { return YearMonth.parse(value, FORMAT); } catch (DateTimeParseException e) { throw new ConversionException(e) .setResourceKey("YearMonthConverter") .setVariable("format", "MM/yyyy"); } } @Override public String convertToString(YearMonth value, Locale locale) { return FORMAT.format(value); } } An empty text field becomes null before your converter is called, so convertToObject only sees real input. Both methods get the locale of the session, for types whose format depends on the language.

page: Create a project from the quickstart archetype
title: Create a project from the quickstart archetype
text: Generate a ready-to-run Wicket project with Maven, know what is in it, and open it in your IDE.
keywords: new project archetype mvn archetype:generate quickstart Maven skeleton scaffold Eclipse IntelliJ IDEA NetBeans VS Code Jetty Start class
body: Use the quickstart archetype when you start a new Wicket application or need a small project to reproduce a bug. It gives you a Maven project with an application class, a home page, a test and an embedded Jetty server.

page: Create a project from the quickstart archetype
title: Adjust the generated project
text: Uncomment wicket-extensions in pom.xml when you need its components, such as data tables, modal dialogs or tabs. Wicket modules lists what each module offers, a
body: Uncomment wicket-extensions in pom.xml when you need its components, such as data tables, modal dialogs or tabs. Wicket modules lists what each module offers, and Maven dependencies shows the dependency for each. Replace slf4j-simple with the logging back end your organization uses. The content security policy in init() allows Google Fonts only because the generated home page uses them. When you replace the page, remove the two Google entries, but keep STYLE_SRC with SELF as long as your pages load stylesheets such as style.css from the application. See Configure the Content Security Policy. For a step-by-step walk through the generated project, follow the tutorial Build your first application.

page: Create a project from the quickstart archetype
title: Generate the project
text: Run the archetype with the Maven coordinates of your project. The groupId also becomes the Java package: mvn archetype:generate \ -DarchetypeGroupId=org.apache.
apis: DarchetypeGroupId DarchetypeArtifactId DarchetypeVersion DgroupId DartifactId DinteractiveMode
body: Run the archetype with the Maven coordinates of your project. The groupId also becomes the Java package: mvn archetype:generate \ -DarchetypeGroupId=org.apache.wicket \ -DarchetypeArtifactId=wicket-archetype-quickstart \ -DarchetypeVersion=10.12.0 \ -DgroupId=com.mycompany \ -DartifactId=myproject \ -DinteractiveMode=false Set archetypeVersion to the Wicket version you build on: 10.12.0 for Wicket 10, which needs Java 17. The quick start writes the command for you. To try an unreleased -SNAPSHOT version, Maven must know the Apache snapshot repository: add it to a profile in your ~/.m2/settings.xml, as described under snapshot versions.

title: Open it in your IDE
text: All current Java IDEs import Maven projects directly: IntelliJ IDEA: choose File, Open, and select the project folder or its pom.xml. Eclipse: choose File, Impo
body: All current Java IDEs import Maven projects directly: IntelliJ IDEA: choose File, Open, and select the project folder or its pom.xml. Eclipse: choose File, Import, Existing Maven Projects, and select the project folder. NetBeans: choose File, Open Project, and select the project folder. VS Code with the Java extensions: open the project folder. A Wicket plugin lets IntelliJ IDEA and Eclipse jump between a component and its markup; see Add Wicket support to your IDE.

page: Create a project from the quickstart archetype
title: Run it
text: Run the main method of Start from your IDE, then open http://localhost:8080. The application runs in development mode, which Start sets with the system property
body: Run the main method of Start from your IDE, then open http://localhost:8080. The application runs in development mode, which Start sets with the system property wicket.configuration. Run the generated test with: mvn test Build a WAR file for an application server with mvn package. Before you deploy it, switch to deployment mode.

page: Create a project from the quickstart archetype
title: What the project contains
text: Maven creates a folder named after the artifactId: File What it is pom.xml Dependencies on wicket-core and wicket-native-websocket-javax, an SLF4J logger, and w
apis: WicketApplication HomePage WicketFilter Start TestHomePage WicketTester
body: Maven creates a folder named after the artifactId: File What it is pom.xml Dependencies on wicket-core and wicket-native-websocket-javax, an SLF4J logger, and wicket-tester, JUnit and Jetty for tests. It also copies the HTML files in src/main/java into the build. src/main/java/.../WicketApplication.java The application class: home page and configuration in init(). It adds the application’s own stylesheets and Google Fonts to the content security policy. src/main/java/.../HomePage.java and HomePage.html The home page, a class and its markup side by side. src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml Registers WicketFilter for all URLs and names the application class. src/main/webapp/style.css, logo.png Static files the home page uses. src/test/java/.../Start.java Starts Jetty with the application on port 8080, and on 8443 with HTTPS. src/test/java/.../TestHomePage.java A WicketTester test that renders the home page. src/test/jetty/*.xml, src/test/resources/keystore Jetty configuration and a self-signed certificate for HTTPS on your machine. Start and Jetty live in the test sources, so they are not packaged in the WAR file that mvn package builds.

page: Isolate the page with COOP and COEP
title: Isolate the page with COOP and COEP
text: Set the Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy and Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy headers, which Wicket sends by default, to isolate your pages from other origins.
keywords: COOP COEP Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy cross-origin isolated SharedArrayBuffer Spectre require-corp window.opener popup
apis: CrossOriginOpenerPolicyConfiguration CrossOriginEmbedderPolicyConfiguration CrossOriginOpenerPolicyRequestCycleListener CrossOriginEmbedderPolicyRequestCycleListener SecuritySettings SharedArrayBuffer Cross Origin Opener Policy Embedder Resource
body: You need this when a page must be cross-origin isolated, for example to use SharedArrayBuffer or performance.measureMemory(), or when the default headers break a popup or an embedded resource. Two response headers control the isolation: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy (COOP) puts your page in its own browsing context group, so a window from another origin that opened it, or that it opened, gets no reference to it. Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy (COEP) with require-corp lets the page load cross-origin resources only when they allow it, through CORS or a Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy header. A page is cross-origin isolated when both are enforced. The isolation protects against side-channel attacks such as Spectre; MDN’s pages on COOP and COEP describe the details.

page: Isolate the page with COOP and COEP
title: Exempt part of the application
text: Both setters take exempted paths after the mode. Responses for an exempted path get no header: getSecuritySettings().setCrossOriginEmbedderPolicyConfiguration(C
body: Both setters take exempted paths after the mode. Responses for an exempted path get no header: getSecuritySettings().setCrossOriginEmbedderPolicyConfiguration(CoepMode.ENFORCING, "/legacy"); Wicket compares each exemption exactly with the context path of the request, HttpServletRequest.getContextPath(), so an exemption applies to a whole web application deployed under that path, not to a single page.

page: Isolate the page with COOP and COEP
title: Keep a popup working
text: A page that opens a window with window.open and keeps using the reference to it, such as a sign-in popup of an identity provider, loses that reference under sam
body: A page that opens a window with window.open and keeps using the reference to it, such as a sign-in popup of an identity provider, loses that reference under same-origin. Use SAME_ORIGIN_ALLOW_POPUPS for the application: getSecuritySettings().setCrossOriginOpenerPolicyConfiguration(CoopMode.SAME_ORIGIN_ALLOW_POPUPS);

page: Isolate the page with COOP and COEP
title: Know the defaults
text: Without any configuration Wicket adds both headers to every response: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy-Report-Only: require-
apis: Cross Origin Opener Policy Embedder Report Only
body: Without any configuration Wicket adds both headers to every response: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy-Report-Only: require-corp COOP is enforced. COEP only reports, so the browser loads everything and tells you what it would have blocked.

page: Isolate the page with COOP and COEP
title: Set the policies
text: Configure both in init(). Wicket reads the settings once, at the end of initialization, and adds a request cycle listener for each policy that is not disabled.
apis: Override CoopMode CoepMode Cross Origin Embedder Policy Report Only
body: Configure both in init(). Wicket reads the settings once, at the end of initialization, and adds a request cycle listener for each policy that is not disabled. Changing them later has no effect. WicketApplication.java @Override protected void init() { super.init(); getSecuritySettings() .setCrossOriginOpenerPolicyConfiguration(CoopMode.SAME_ORIGIN) .setCrossOriginEmbedderPolicyConfiguration(CoepMode.ENFORCING); } With COEP enforced, check that every cross-origin image, font, script and frame the pages use still loads. COOP modes CoopMode Header value Effect SAME_ORIGIN (default) same-origin Only same-origin documents share the browsing context group SAME_ORIGIN_ALLOW_POPUPS same-origin-allow-popups As same-origin, but popups the page opens keep their reference to it UNSAFE_NONE unsafe-none No isolation; the browser default DISABLED (no header) Wicket sends no COOP header COEP modes CoepMode Header Effect REPORTING (default) Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy-Report-Only: require-corp Violations are reported, nothing is blocked ENFORCING Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp Cross-origin resources without permission are blocked DISABLED (no header) Wicket sends no COEP header
