title: Turn the headers off
text: getSecuritySettings() .setCrossOriginOpenerPolicyConfiguration(CoopMode.DISABLED) .setCrossOriginEmbedderPolicyConfiguration(CoepMode.DISABLED); Do this when a
body: getSecuritySettings() .setCrossOriginOpenerPolicyConfiguration(CoopMode.DISABLED) .setCrossOriginEmbedderPolicyConfiguration(CoepMode.DISABLED); Do this when a proxy or the container already sets these headers, so that responses do not carry two different values.

title: Configure the Content Security Policy
text: Work with the strict Content Security Policy Wicket sends by default, allow extra sources, report violations, and move inline scripts and styles out of the markup.
keywords: CSP Content-Security-Policy nonce unsafe-inline strict-dynamic XSS inline script onclick style attribute script-src-attr style-src-attr report-uri Refused to execute inline script
apis: ContentSecurityPolicySettings CSPHeaderConfiguration CSPDirective CSPDirectiveSrcValue OnEventHeaderItem ReportCSPViolationMapper WebPage Content Security Policy WebApplication
body: You need this when the browser refuses a script, a stylesheet or an inline style on your pages, or when you want to tighten or loosen the policy. Every WebPage is sent with a Content-Security-Policy header. By default it is this strict policy, with a fresh nonce for every request: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'strict-dynamic' 'nonce-XYZ'; style-src 'nonce-XYZ'; img-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; manifest-src 'self'; child-src 'self'; base-uri 'self' Scripts and stylesheets only run when they carry the nonce. Wicket adds it to everything you contribute through renderHead. Images, fonts, frames and Ajax calls are allowed from your own origin. Anything inline is blocked: <script> and <style> in the markup, onclick and other event attributes, and style attributes. How Wicket keeps applications secure explains why the policy has no 'unsafe-inline'. All settings live in getCspSettings() of your WebApplication. Change them in init(), after super.init().

title: Allow a source
text: Add sources to a directive of the enforced (blocking()) policy: WicketApplication.java @Override protected void init() { super.init(); getCspSettings().blocking
body: Add sources to a directive of the enforced (blocking()) policy: WicketApplication.java @Override protected void init() { super.init(); getCspSettings().blocking() .add(CSPDirective.IMG_SRC, "data:") .add(CSPDirective.FONT_SRC, "https://fonts.gstatic.com") .add(CSPDirective.STYLE_SRC, "https://fonts.googleapis.com/css"); } CSPDirective has a constant for every directive, CSPDirectiveSrcValue for keywords such as SELF, NONE and UNSAFE_INLINE. Scripts cannot be allowed by URL: 'strict-dynamic' makes browsers ignore URL sources in script-src. Load them through a header item instead.

title: Allow inline images, external images and media
text: img-src 'self' only allows images from your own origin. Images embedded as data: URLs, such as those of InlineImage or base64 images in a stylesheet, need data:
body: img-src 'self' only allows images from your own origin. Images embedded as data: URLs, such as those of InlineImage or base64 images in a stylesheet, need data:; images from another host need that host. There is no media-src, so default-src 'none' blocks every <video> and <audio> source until you add one: getCspSettings().blocking() .add(CSPDirective.IMG_SRC, "data:", "https://images.example.com") .add(CSPDirective.MEDIA_SRC, CSPDirectiveSrcValue.SELF);

title: Exclude pages from the policy
text: A page writes the header only when the request is handled by a RenderPageRequestHandler. The protected filter decides which of those requests get it: a Predicat
body: A page writes the header only when the request is handled by a RenderPageRequestHandler. The protected filter decides which of those requests get it: a Predicate<IRequestHandler> that tests the handler. Change the filter to leave pages out: getCspSettings().setProtectedFilter(handler -> !(handler instanceof RenderPageRequestHandler h && h.getPageClass() == LegacyReportPage.class)); setProtectedFilter(Predicate<IRequestHandler>) is deprecated since 10.11.0. For responses other than page renders, Wicket also has a CSPRequestCycleListener.

title: Load CSS and JavaScript through header items
text: A <link> or <script> written in the markup gets no nonce. Contribute it from the component instead, and Wicket adds the nonce: MyPanel.java @Override public voi
apis: Override IHeaderResponse CssHeaderItem CssResourceReference MyPanel JavaScriptHeaderItem JavaScriptResourceReference
body: A <link> or <script> written in the markup gets no nonce. Contribute it from the component instead, and Wicket adds the nonce: MyPanel.java @Override public void renderHead(IHeaderResponse response) { super.renderHead(response); response.render(CssHeaderItem.forReference( new CssResourceReference(MyPanel.class, "my-panel.css"))); response.render(JavaScriptHeaderItem.forReference( new JavaScriptResourceReference(MyPanel.class, "my-panel.js"))); } A stylesheet or script inside <wicket:link> that Wicket turns into a package resource URL also gets the nonce. Scripts loaded this way may load further scripts, because of 'strict-dynamic'. Add CSS and JavaScript to a page covers the header items.

title: Loosen or turn off the policy
text: unsafeInline() replaces the policy with a preset that allows inline scripts and styles and eval. It removes most of what CSP protects against, but it can be a f
body: unsafeInline() replaces the policy with a preset that allows inline scripts and styles and eval. It removes most of what CSP protects against, but it can be a first step for an application that is not ready for the strict policy: getCspSettings().blocking().unsafeInline(); To send no policy at all: getCspSettings().blocking().disabled(); strict() restores the default.

title: Replace inline event handlers
text: Move an onclick or onsubmit attribute into an OnEventHeaderItem. Wicket renders it as a script with the nonce that attaches the handler: @Override public void r
body: Move an onclick or onsubmit attribute into an OnEventHeaderItem. Wicket renders it as a script with the nonce that attaches the handler: @Override public void renderHead(IHeaderResponse response) { super.renderHead(response); response.render(OnEventHeaderItem.forComponent(this, "submit", "return confirm('Do you really want to submit?');")); } The component needs a markup id, so call setOutputMarkupId(true) on it. The same applies to an AttributeModifier that writes an event attribute.

title: Replace style attributes
text: Put the styling in a stylesheet and switch CSS classes, for example with AttributeModifier.append("class", "warning") instead of a modifier on style. Scripts th
body: Put the styling in a stylesheet and switch CSS classes, for example with AttributeModifier.append("class", "warning") instead of a modifier on style. Scripts that set the style attribute in generated markup have to set the style DOM property instead, which the policy allows. If you cannot remove the style attributes yet, allow them on their own and keep the nonce for stylesheets: getCspSettings().blocking().add(CSPDirective.STYLE_SRC_ATTR, CSPDirectiveSrcValue.UNSAFE_INLINE); style-src-attr only governs style attributes, so <style> elements still need the nonce. SCRIPT_SRC_ATTR does the same for event handler attributes, but allowing those removes most of the protection against script injection.

title: Report violations to the application
text: reportBack() adds a report-uri that points to an endpoint in your application. Wicket logs every report it receives at error level, through the logger org.apach
body: reportBack() adds a report-uri that points to an endpoint in your application. Wicket logs every report it receives at error level, through the logger org.apache.wicket.csp.ReportCSPViolationMapper. if (usesDevelopmentConfig()) { getCspSettings().blocking().reportBack(); } The endpoint is open to anyone and every report ends up in your log. On a production system, limit the size of that log, or use reportBackAt(path) or add(CSPDirective.REPORT_URI, url) to send reports elsewhere.

title: Try a policy before you enforce it
text: reporting() configures a second policy, sent as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only. Browsers report what it would block without blocking anything: getCspSettin
body: reporting() configures a second policy, sent as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only. Browsers report what it would block without blocking anything: getCspSettings().reporting() .strict() .reportBack();

title: Protect against cross-site request forgery
text: Refuse link clicks, form submits and Ajax calls that another site makes on behalf of your users, with ResourceIsolationRequestCycleListener.
keywords: CSRF XSRF Sec-Fetch-Site fetch metadata Origin header Referer cross-origin same-site 403 Forbidden CsrfPreventionRequestCycleListener cross-site WebSocket hijacking
apis: ResourceIsolationRequestCycleListener FetchMetadataResourceIsolationPolicy OriginResourceIsolationPolicy IResourceIsolationPolicy WebSocketAwareResourceIsolationRequestCycleListener WebSocketConnectionOriginFilter CryptoMapper
body: You need this when a page on another site must not be able to make your users click a link, submit a form or fire an Ajax call in your application. Browsers send your session cookie along with such forged requests, so the request has to be checked for where it came from. How Wicket keeps applications secure explains what stateful pages and encrypted URLs already do against it.

title: Accept a trusted origin
text: For clients without fetch metadata, OriginResourceIsolationPolicy.addAcceptedOrigin("partner.example.com") accepts requests from that host and every host below
body: For clients without fetch metadata, OriginResourceIsolationPolicy.addAcceptedOrigin("partner.example.com") accepts requests from that host and every host below it.

title: Allow requests from your other subdomains
text: Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site means a different origin on the same registrable domain, such as shop.example.com calling app.example.com. It is refused by default. I
apis: Sec Fetch Site ResourceIsolationRequestCycleListener FetchMetadataResourceIsolationPolicy OriginResourceIsolationPolicy
body: Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site means a different origin on the same registrable domain, such as shop.example.com calling app.example.com. It is refused by default. If every origin on your site is part of the same application, allow it: getRequestCycleListeners().add(new ResourceIsolationRequestCycleListener( new FetchMetadataResourceIsolationPolicy().setSameSiteAllowed(true), new OriginResourceIsolationPolicy())); This trusts every subdomain. A hostile sibling origin, through a subdomain takeover, user-provided content or an XSS hole elsewhere on the site, can then act on behalf of your users. Wicket 10 releases before 10.11.0 allowed same-site requests without this setting.

title: Change what happens to a refused request
text: Setting Default Effect setDisallowedOutcomeAction(CsrfAction) ABORT What to do when a policy refuses the request setUnknownOutcomeAction(CsrfAction) ABORT What
body: Setting Default Effect setDisallowedOutcomeAction(CsrfAction) ABORT What to do when a policy refuses the request setUnknownOutcomeAction(CsrfAction) ABORT What to do when no policy can decide setErrorCode(int) 403 Status code for ABORT setErrorMessage(String) “The request was blocked by a resource isolation policy” Message for ABORT CsrfAction.ABORT answers with the error code, SUPPRESS renders the targeted page without invoking the listener, and ALLOW logs the request and lets it through. ALLOW is useful to try the listener out on a running application before you enforce it.

title: Check page renders as well
text: Override isChecked(IRequestHandler) to return true for every page request handler. Policies then also see renders, and FetchMetadataResourceIsolationPolicy stil
body: Override isChecked(IRequestHandler) to return true for every page request handler. Policies then also see renders, and FetchMetadataResourceIsolationPolicy still allows a plain top-level navigation from another site. var listener = new ResourceIsolationRequestCycleListener() { @Override protected boolean isChecked(IRequestHandler handler) { return handler instanceof IPageRequestHandler; } };

title: Combine it with encrypted URLs
text: CryptoMapper and this listener work independently and can be combined. CsrfPreventionRequestCycleListener, the Origin-header check of Wicket 7 to 9, was removed
body: CryptoMapper and this listener work independently and can be combined. CsrfPreventionRequestCycleListener, the Origin-header check of Wicket 7 to 9, was removed in Wicket 10; OriginResourceIsolationPolicy contains its logic.

title: Exempt a path or a page
text: var listener = new ResourceIsolationRequestCycleListener() { @Override protected boolean isChecked(IRequestablePage targetedPage) { return !(targetedPage instan
body: var listener = new ResourceIsolationRequestCycleListener() { @Override protected boolean isChecked(IRequestablePage targetedPage) { return !(targetedPage instanceof PartnerCallbackPage); } }; listener.addExemptedPaths("/api/callback"); getRequestCycleListeners().add(listener); An exempted path is compared exactly with the path info of the request, HttpServletRequest.getPathInfo().

title: Keep your tests passing
text: WicketTester sends no Sec-Fetch-Site header, so with the listener registered its requests are refused. Set the header before clicking a link or submitting a for
body: WicketTester sends no Sec-Fetch-Site header, so with the listener registered its requests are refused. Set the header before clicking a link or submitting a form: tester.addRequestHeader(FetchMetadataResourceIsolationPolicy.SEC_FETCH_SITE_HEADER, FetchMetadataResourceIsolationPolicy.SAME_ORIGIN); tester.clickLink("delete"); A request header applies to the next request only. Test pages and components has more on headers in tests.

title: Protect WebSocket connections
text: With native WebSockets, register WebSocketAwareResourceIsolationRequestCycleListener instead. It checks the HTTP request that opens the connection, which carrie
body: With native WebSockets, register WebSocketAwareResourceIsolationRequestCycleListener instead. It checks the HTTP request that opens the connection, which carries Origin and fetch metadata headers, and skips the messages that arrive over the open connection, which carry no headers: getRequestCycleListeners().add(new WebSocketAwareResourceIsolationRequestCycleListener()); Browsers let any page open a WebSocket to any host, and send your cookies with it. To accept connections only from your own pages, also install a WebSocketConnectionOriginFilter with the exact origins that may connect: WebSocketSettings.Holder.get(this).setConnectionFilter( new WebSocketConnectionOriginFilter(List.of("https://app.example.com"))); A connection whose single Origin header is not in the list is closed with code 1008, “Origin mismatch”. An empty list allows every origin. Push updates over a WebSocket covers the setup.

title: Register the listener
text: WicketApplication.java @Override protected void init() { super.init(); getRequestCycleListeners().add(new ResourceIsolationRequestCycleListener()); } The listen
body: WicketApplication.java @Override protected void init() { super.init(); getRequestCycleListeners().add(new ResourceIsolationRequestCycleListener()); } The listener is not registered by default. Once it is, every request that invokes a listener on a page (a Link.onClick(), a Form.onSubmit(), an Ajax behavior) is checked. A refused request ends with 403 Forbidden. Requests that only render a page are not checked, so other sites can still link to your pages.

title: What the default policies check
text: Without arguments the listener asks two policies, in order, and the first answer other than “unknown” decides: FetchMetadataResourceIsolationPolicy reads the Se
apis: FetchMetadataResourceIsolationPolicy Sec Fetch Site OriginResourceIsolationPolicy Origin Referer ResourceIsolationRequestCycleListener
body: Without arguments the listener asks two policies, in order, and the first answer other than “unknown” decides: FetchMetadataResourceIsolationPolicy reads the Sec-Fetch-Site header that browsers add to every request. It allows same-origin and none (a typed URL or a bookmark). A request from another origin may render a page through a plain top-level navigation, but may not invoke a listener. OriginResourceIsolationPolicy compares the Origin or Referer header with the requested URL. It only gets a say when a request has no Sec-Fetch-Site header, which current browsers always send. When neither policy can decide, the request is refused. To rely on fetch metadata alone, pass the policy yourself: getRequestCycleListeners().add( new ResourceIsolationRequestCycleListener(new FetchMetadataResourceIsolationPolicy()));

title: Generate a resource in code
text: Build files on request, such as a CSV export, a PDF or an image, by extending AbstractResource or writing a lambda, and offer them for download with ResourceLink.
keywords: dynamic resource download export CSV PDF generate file file download attachment Content-Disposition content type newResourceResponse writeData lambda resource
apis: AbstractResource ResourceResponse WriteCallback IResource ResourceLink ByteArrayResource DynamicImageResource ContentDisposition ResourceReference
body: Write a resource when the application has to hand out a file that does not exist until someone asks for it: an export of the rows on screen, a generated invoice, a chart. A resource answers its own request, so it can write any content type, outside the page.

title: Generate an image
text: DynamicImageResource turns bytes into an image response; implement getImageData. Use toImageData to encode a BufferedImage in the format you pass to the constru
apis: DynamicImageResource BufferedImage BadgeImage Override Attributes Graphics2D Level Image
body: DynamicImageResource turns bytes into an image response; implement getImageData. Use toImageData to encode a BufferedImage in the format you pass to the constructor: public class BadgeImage extends DynamicImageResource { private final int level; public BadgeImage(int level) { super("png"); this.level = level; } @Override protected byte[] getImageData(Attributes attributes) { BufferedImage image = new BufferedImage(120, 30, BufferedImage.TYPE_INT_ARGB); Graphics2D g = image.createGraphics(); g.drawString("Level " + level, 10, 20); g.dispose(); return toImageData(image); } } Pass it to an Image: add(new Image("badge", new BadgeImage(3))).

title: Offer it as a download link
text: Give a ResourceLink the resource: OrdersPage.java add(new ResourceLink<Void>("export", new OrdersCsvResource())); OrdersPage.html <a wicket:id="export">Download
body: Give a ResourceLink the resource: OrdersPage.java add(new ResourceLink("export", new OrdersCsvResource())); OrdersPage.html Download as CSV The resource is stored in the link and the link’s URL points at the page, which makes the page stateful. To keep the page stateless, or to give the file a URL that works without the page, link to a resource reference instead: private static final ResourceReference ORDERS_CSV = ResourceReference.of("orders.csv", OrdersCsvResource::new); add(new ResourceLink("export", ORDERS_CSV)); ResourceReference.of creates a reference whose resource comes from the supplier. The link registers the reference with the application when it renders; to choose the URL yourself, mount the reference as in Give a resource a URL. A reference serves all users, so the resource must find the current user’s data while it responds, as the example does, and not hold it in a field.

title: Serve bytes you already have
text: When the content is already in a byte array, for example a PDF from a report library, use ByteArrayResource with the content type and an optional file name: byt
body: When the content is already in a byte array, for example a PDF from a report library, use ByteArrayResource with the content type and an optional file name: byte[] pdf = invoiceService.render(invoiceId); add(new ResourceLink<Void>("invoice", new ByteArrayResource("application/pdf", pdf, "invoice-" + invoiceId + ".pdf"))); The byte array becomes part of the link and is serialized with the page, so keep this for small files. For a file on disk, DownloadLink takes a File or a model of one.

title: Write a resource as a lambda
text: IResource has a single method, so a small resource can be a lambda that writes to the response: IResource ping = attributes -> attributes.getResponse().write("p
body: IResource has a single method, so a small resource can be a lambda that writes to the response: IResource ping = attributes -> attributes.getResponse().write("pong"); A lambda sets no content type, file name or cache headers. Use it for plain text or for tests, and AbstractResource for anything a browser should handle properly.

title: Write the resource
text: Extend AbstractResource and implement newResourceResponse. Describe the response in a ResourceResponse and write the content in a WriteCallback: OrdersCsvResour
apis: AbstractResource ResourceResponse WriteCallback OrdersCsvResource Override Attributes ContentDisposition IOException List Order OrderService StringBuilder StandardCharsets
body: Extend AbstractResource and implement newResourceResponse. Describe the response in a ResourceResponse and write the content in a WriteCallback: OrdersCsvResource.java public class OrdersCsvResource extends AbstractResource { @Override protected ResourceResponse newResourceResponse(Attributes attributes) { ResourceResponse response = new ResourceResponse(); response.setContentType("text/csv"); response.setTextEncoding("UTF-8"); response.setFileName("orders.csv"); response.setContentDisposition(ContentDisposition.ATTACHMENT); response.disableCaching(); response.setWriteCallback(new WriteCallback() { @Override public void writeData(Attributes attributes) throws IOException { List<Order> orders = OrderService.get().findForCurrentUser(); StringBuilder csv = new StringBuilder("number;date;total\n"); for (Order order : orders) { csv.append(order.getNumber()).append(';') .append(order.getDate()).append(';') .append(order.getTotal()).append('\n'); } attributes.getResponse().write(csv.toString().getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)); } }); return response; } } ContentDisposition.ATTACHMENT makes the browser save the file under the name from setFileName; INLINE shows it in the browser when it can. Wicket calls writeData only when the content has to be sent, so do the expensive work there. For large output, write to attributes.getResponse().getOutputStream() instead of building it in memory. To refuse a request, return a response with an error code, for example new ResourceResponse().setError(404).

page: Load texts from your own source
title: Load texts from your own source
text: Add a string resource loader that reads texts from a database or an existing Java ResourceBundle, and change the chain of loaders Wicket searches.
keywords: database translations messages from database ResourceBundle string resource loader custom localization translation service nested keys clear localization cache
apis: IStringResourceLoader ResourceSettings BundleStringResourceLoader NestedStringResourceLoader Localizer PackageStringResourceLoader ResourceBundle
body: Add your own string resource loader when texts do not come from properties files next to your classes: translations kept in a database so that editors can change them, an existing Java ResourceBundle shared with other applications, or a translation service. Wicket asks its loaders in turn until one returns a text; see Where Wicket looks for texts for the default chain.

page: Load texts from your own source
title: Make changed texts visible
text: The Localizer caches every lookup by key, component path, locale, style and variation, including lookups that found nothing. When a text in your source changes,
body: The Localizer caches every lookup by key, component path, locale, style and variation, including lookups that found nothing. When a text in your source changes, clear the cache: Localizer.get().clearCache(); Localizer#setEnableCache(false) turns the cache off, which helps while you edit texts during development and costs a lookup in every loader on every request.

page: Load texts from your own source
title: Refer to other keys from a text
text: NestedStringResourceLoader wraps a list of loaders and replaces references to other keys inside a text. You choose the syntax with a regular expression whose fi
apis: NestedStringResourceLoader List IStringResourceLoader Pattern Acme Shop Welcome
body: NestedStringResourceLoader wraps a list of loaders and replaces references to other keys inside a text. You choose the syntax with a regular expression whose first group is the key: List<IStringResourceLoader> loaders = getResourceSettings().getStringResourceLoaders(); NestedStringResourceLoader nested = new NestedStringResourceLoader(loaders, Pattern.compile("#\\(([^ ]*?)\\)")); loaders.clear(); loaders.add(nested); app.name=Acme Shop welcome=Welcome to #(app.name)! When a referenced key is not found, the whole text is not found.

page: Load texts from your own source
title: Register the loader
text: Add the loader to the list in the resource settings, in the init() method of your application. The position decides its priority: @Override protected void init(
body: Add the loader to the list in the resource settings, in the init() method of your application. The position decides its priority: @Override protected void init() { super.init(); List<IStringResourceLoader> loaders = getResourceSettings().getStringResourceLoaders(); // database texts override the properties files loaders.add(0, new DatabaseStringResourceLoader(translationRepository)); // or: properties files first, database as a fallback // loaders.add(new DatabaseStringResourceLoader(translationRepository)); } The list is modifiable, so you can also remove a default loader, or clear it and build your own chain.

page: Load texts from your own source
title: Rename the package bundle files
text: Package bundles are called wicket-package.properties. To use another name, replace the PackageStringResourceLoader in the list with one that has another file na
body: Package bundles are called wicket-package.properties. To use another name, replace the PackageStringResourceLoader in the list with one that has another file name: PackageStringResourceLoader packageLoader = new PackageStringResourceLoader(); packageLoader.setFilename("messages"); List<IStringResourceLoader> loaders = getResourceSettings().getStringResourceLoaders(); loaders.replaceAll(loader -> loader instanceof PackageStringResourceLoader ? packageLoader : loader);

page: Load texts from your own source
title: Reuse an existing Java ResourceBundle
text: BundleStringResourceLoader reads texts from a standard ResourceBundle by its base name, with Java’s own lookup by locale: getResourceSettings().getStringResourc
body: BundleStringResourceLoader reads texts from a standard ResourceBundle by its base name, with Java’s own lookup by locale: getResourceSettings().getStringResourceLoaders() .add(new BundleStringResourceLoader("com.example.i18n.Messages")); It ignores style, variation and the component.

page: Load texts from your own source
title: Write a loader
text: Implement IStringResourceLoader. It has two methods: one that gets the component asking for the text, and one that gets only a class. Return null when you have
apis: IStringResourceLoader DatabaseStringResourceLoader TranslationRepository Override String Class Locale Component
body: Implement IStringResourceLoader. It has two methods: one that gets the component asking for the text, and one that gets only a class. Return null when you have no text for the key, so that the next loader gets its turn. Do not throw an exception for a missing key. DatabaseStringResourceLoader.java public class DatabaseStringResourceLoader implements IStringResourceLoader { private final TranslationRepository translations; public DatabaseStringResourceLoader(TranslationRepository translations) { this.translations = translations; } @Override public String loadStringResource(Class<?> clazz, String key, Locale locale, String style, String variation) { return translations.find(key, locale).orElse(null); } @Override public String loadStringResource(Component component, String key, Locale locale, String style, String variation) { return loadStringResource(component != null ? component.getClass() : null, key, locale, style, variation); } } TranslationRepository stands for your own data access. Wicket passes the locale as it is, for example de_CH. Falling back from de_CH to de and then to a default text is up to the repository. The locale, style and variation are already resolved from the component; use the arguments, not the component, to read them.

page: Switch between development and deployment mode
title: Switch between development and deployment mode
text: Run Wicket in deployment mode on production servers, with a system property, a web.xml parameter or code, and check which mode is active.
keywords: production DEPLOYMENT DEVELOPMENT wicket.configuration configuration parameter WARNING Wicket is running in DEVELOPMENT mode getConfigurationType usesDevelopmentConfig context-param init-param system property
apis: RuntimeConfigurationType WebApplication Application Wicket Do See
body: Switch to deployment mode before an application goes to a production server. Wicket starts in development mode unless you tell it otherwise. That mode shows full stack traces to visitors, polls markup files for changes and adds the Ajax debug window, so you do not want it in production. Application settings lists every setting the mode changes. You can recognize development mode by this warning on standard error when the application starts: ******************************************************************** *** WARNING: Wicket is running in DEVELOPMENT mode. *** *** ^^^^^^^^^^^ *** *** Do NOT deploy to your live server(s) without changing this. *** *** See Application#getConfigurationType() for more information. *** ********************************************************************

page: Switch between development and deployment mode
title: Check which mode is active
text: When it starts, Wicket logs the mode at INFO level: [wicket.myproject] Started Wicket version 10.12.0 in DEPLOYMENT mode In code, ask the application: if (getAp
body: When it starts, Wicket logs the mode at INFO level: [wicket.myproject] Started Wicket version 10.12.0 in DEPLOYMENT mode In code, ask the application: if (getApplication().usesDevelopmentConfig()) { add(new DebugBar("debug")); } DebugBar comes from the wicket-devutils module. usesDeploymentConfig() is the opposite check. The Start class of the quickstart sets wicket.configuration to development, so an application you run from your IDE stays in development mode whatever web.xml says.

page: Switch between development and deployment mode
title: Set the mode in code
text: Override getConfigurationType() in your application class when the application decides for itself, for example from an environment variable: public class Wicket
body: Override getConfigurationType() in your application class when the application decides for itself, for example from an environment variable: public class WicketApplication extends WebApplication { @Override public RuntimeConfigurationType getConfigurationType() { return "production".equals(System.getenv("APP_ENV")) ? RuntimeConfigurationType.DEPLOYMENT : RuntimeConfigurationType.DEVELOPMENT; } } The override replaces the lookup of the system property and the web.xml parameters. WebApplication also has setConfigurationType(), but you can call it only once, and only before Wicket initializes the application.

page: Switch between development and deployment mode
title: Set the mode in web.xml
text: Add a configuration parameter to the Wicket filter: <filter> <filter-name>wicket.myproject</filter-name> <filter-class>org.apache.wicket.protocol.http.WicketFil
body: Add a configuration parameter to the Wicket filter: <filter> <filter-name>wicket.myproject</filter-name> <filter-class>org.apache.wicket.protocol.http.WicketFilter</filter-class> <init-param> <param-name>applicationClassName</param-name> <param-value>com.mycompany.WicketApplication</param-value> </init-param> <init-param> <param-name>configuration</param-name> <param-value>deployment</param-value> </init-param> </filter> Or set it for the whole web application as a context parameter: <context-param> <param-name>configuration</param-name> <param-value>deployment</param-value> </context-param> Both places also accept the name wicket.configuration. When Wicket finds more than one setting, it uses the first of: the system property, then wicket.configuration as filter and as context parameter, then configuration as filter and as context parameter.

page: Switch between development and deployment mode
title: Set the mode with a system property
text: Start the JVM of the server with the system property wicket.configuration: java -Dwicket.configuration=deployment ... For Tomcat, put it in CATALINA_OPTS, for e
body: Start the JVM of the server with the system property wicket.configuration: java -Dwicket.configuration=deployment ... For Tomcat, put it in CATALINA_OPTS, for example in bin/setenv.sh. A system property overrides the parameters in web.xml, so the same WAR file runs in development mode on your machine and in deployment mode on the server. The value is not case-sensitive.

page: Load data once per request with detachable models
title: Load data once per request with detachable models
text: Keep only an id in the page and load the entity fresh in every request with LoadableDetachableModel.
keywords: LDM entity model JPA Hibernate database load detach onDetach transient NotSerializableException LazyInitializationException page size
body: Use a detachable model for data that comes from a database or a service. The model loads the object the first time a component asks for it in a request, drops it at the end of the request, and keeps only what it needs to load it again. The page stays small, and every request sees current data. Models and component data explains why this matters. The examples get their service through an injected field, as described in Inject Spring beans. Injected fields hold a serializable proxy, so a lambda can use them.

page: Load data once per request with detachable models
title: Detach models the component does not own
text: Wicket detaches the default model of every component. A model that you keep in a field of your component, or that a behavior holds, is detached only if you do i
body: Wicket detaches the default model of every component. A model that you keep in a field of your component, or that a behavior holds, is detached only if you do it yourself. Use more than one model in a component shows how.

page: Load data once per request with detachable models
title: Keep the id of a new entity
text: A form that creates an entity starts with an object that has no id yet. Save it, then remember the id it got, so the model can load it in later requests. Read t
apis: PersonModel LoadableDetachableModel Person SpringBean PersonService Long Injector Override
body: A form that creates an entity starts with an object that has no id yet. Save it, then remember the id it got, so the model can load it in later requests. Read the id from the object when the model is detached: public class PersonModel extends LoadableDetachableModel<Person> { @SpringBean private PersonService personService; private Long id; public PersonModel(Person person) { super(person); this.id = person.getId(); Injector.get().inject(this); } @Override protected Person load() { return id == null ? new Person() : personService.findById(id); } @Override protected void onDetach() { Person person = getObject(); if (person != null) { id = person.getId(); } } } onDetach() runs only when the model held an object in this request. getObject() then returns that object without loading it again. The model does not save anything. Changes made to the object during a request are lost when it is detached, unless your code saved them, usually in the form’s onSubmit().

page: Load data once per request with detachable models
title: Load an entity by id
text: LoadableDetachableModel.of takes a supplier that is called once per request: PersonPage.java public class PersonPage extends WebPage { @SpringBean private Perso
apis: LoadableDetachableModel PersonPage WebPage SpringBean PersonService PageParameters IModel Person Label
body: LoadableDetachableModel.of takes a supplier that is called once per request: PersonPage.java public class PersonPage extends WebPage { @SpringBean private PersonService personService; public PersonPage(PageParameters parameters) { long id = parameters.get("id").toLong(); IModel<Person> person = LoadableDetachableModel.of(() -> personService.findById(id)); add(new Label("name", person.map(Person::getName))); add(new Label("email", person.map(Person::getEmail))); } } Both labels call getObject() while they render. The first call runs the supplier; the second gets the same object. At the end of the request Wicket detaches the labels, which detach their models and so person. The page is stored with the id and the lambda, not with the person.

page: Load data once per request with detachable models
title: Replace the object
text: setObject() puts an object in the model until the end of the request: personModel.setObject(personService.findByEmail(email)); The next request calls load() aga
body: setObject() puts an object in the model until the end of the request: personModel.setObject(personService.findByEmail(email)); The next request calls load() again. If load() uses an id, change the id as well, or the model returns to the old entity. PersonModel above does that in onDetach().

page: Load data once per request with detachable models
title: Use detachable models in repeaters
text: A list of rows needs a detachable model per row, not one model for the whole list. IDataProvider.model(T) is where a data view gets that model; return a PersonM
body: A list of rows needs a detachable model per row, not one model for the whole list. IDataProvider.model(T) is where a data view gets that model; return a PersonModel there. Page through data shows a complete provider.

page: Load data once per request with detachable models
title: Write a reusable model class
text: Subclass LoadableDetachableModel when many pages load the same kind of entity. Pass the loaded object to the constructor when you already have it, so the first
apis: LoadableDetachableModel PersonModel Person SpringBean PersonService Injector Override
body: Subclass LoadableDetachableModel when many pages load the same kind of entity. Pass the loaded object to the constructor when you already have it, so the first request does not load it twice: PersonModel.java public class PersonModel extends LoadableDetachableModel<Person> { @SpringBean private PersonService personService; private final long id; public PersonModel(Person person) { super(person); this.id = person.getId(); Injector.get().inject(this); } @Override protected Person load() { return personService.findById(id); } } Wicket injects @SpringBean fields of components when they are created, but not of other objects such as models. Injector.get().inject(this) fills the field.

page: Let the user pick from a list
title: Let the user pick from a list
text: Show a drop-down list with DropDownChoice, render objects and enums as options, and control the empty "Choose One" option.
keywords: select drop-down dropdown combo box option Choose One choice renderer enum setNullValid
apis: DropDownChoice IChoiceRenderer ChoiceRenderer LambdaChoiceRenderer EnumChoiceRenderer GroupedDropDownChoice
body: You need this when the user picks one value out of a known set: a country, a category, a person. A DropDownChoice renders a <select> with an option per choice, and puts the chosen object, not a string, into its model.

page: Let the user pick from a list
title: Control the empty option
text: While the model is null, the list starts with an option “Choose One”. Once the user has picked a value and the form is saved, that option disappears and the use
body: While the model is null, the list starts with an option “Choose One”. Once the user has picked a value and the form is saved, that option disappears and the user cannot go back to no value. To let the user clear the selection, call setNullValid(true). The empty option is then always there, with an empty text. Neither setting makes a choice mandatory. Call setRequired(true) for that. Change the texts in your properties file. Wicket tries the key prefixed with the component id first: country.null=Pick a country country.nullValid=No country The keys without prefix, null and nullValid, change the text for every drop-down that uses the file.

page: Let the user pick from a list
title: Group the options
text: GroupedDropDownChoice renders <optgroup> elements. Sort the choices by group and implement isNewGroup, hasNoGroup and getGroupLabel to tell where each group sta
body: GroupedDropDownChoice renders <optgroup> elements. Sort the choices by group and implement isNewGroup, hasNoGroup and getGroupLabel to tell where each group starts and what it is called. To let the user pick more than one value, see Select several values. For a few options shown at once, a RadioChoice works the same way as a DropDownChoice.

page: Let the user pick from a list
title: React when the user picks an option
text: Add an AjaxFormComponentUpdatingBehavior on the change event to update other parts of the page as soon as the selection changes, for example to fill a second li
body: Add an AjaxFormComponentUpdatingBehavior on the change event to update other parts of the page as soon as the selection changes, for example to fill a second list with the cities of the chosen country: country.add(AjaxFormComponentUpdatingBehavior.onUpdate("change", target -> target.add(city))); The behavior validates the drop-down and updates its model before your code runs. See Ajax behaviors. Without Ajax, FormComponentUpdatingBehavior does the same with a full page request.

page: Let the user pick from a list
title: Show a list of strings
text: Pass the component a model for the selection and a list of choices, and bind it to a <select> tag. OrderPage.java List<String> sizes = List.of("Small", "Medium"
apis: List String Small Medium Large DropDownChoice LambdaModel Order
body: Pass the component a model for the selection and a list of choices, and bind it to a <select> tag. OrderPage.java List<String> sizes = List.of("Small", "Medium", "Large"); form.add(new DropDownChoice<>("size", LambdaModel.of(order, Order::getSize, Order::setSize), sizes)); OrderPage.html <select wicket:id="size"></select> Wicket renders the options itself; anything you put between the <select> tags is replaced.

page: Let the user pick from a list
title: Show enum values
text: Use EnumChoiceRenderer. It uses the constant name as option value and looks the text up in your resources under <EnumName>.<CONSTANT>: form.add(new DropDownChoi
apis: EnumChoiceRenderer EnumName DropDownChoice LambdaModel Ticket List Priority Low High
body: Use EnumChoiceRenderer. It uses the constant name as option value and looks the text up in your resources under <EnumName>.<CONSTANT>: form.add(new DropDownChoice<>("priority", LambdaModel.of(ticket, Ticket::getPriority, Ticket::setPriority), List.of(Priority.values()), new EnumChoiceRenderer<>(this))); TicketPage.properties Priority.LOW=Low Priority.HIGH=High Passing the component (this) makes the renderer look in the resources of that component and its parents, such as the page’s properties file. Translate the options of a choice has more on translating options.

page: Let the user pick from a list
title: Show objects with a choice renderer
text: For objects other than strings, tell the component what to show and what to use as option value with an IChoiceRenderer. LambdaChoiceRenderer takes a function f
apis: IChoiceRenderer LambdaChoiceRenderer IModel List Country LoadableDetachableModel DropDownChoice LambdaModel Address ChoiceRenderer
body: For objects other than strings, tell the component what to show and what to use as option value with an IChoiceRenderer. LambdaChoiceRenderer takes a function for the text and one for the id: IModel<List<Country>> countries = LoadableDetachableModel.of(countryService::findAll); form.add(new DropDownChoice<>("country", LambdaModel.of(address, Address::getCountry, Address::setCountry), countries, new LambdaChoiceRenderer<>(Country::getName, Country::getIsoCode))); ChoiceRenderer does the same with property expressions: new ChoiceRenderer<>("name", "isoCode"). Give the renderer an id whenever the list can change between rendering and submitting, such as a list loaded from a database. Without an id, the option value is the position in the list, and a changed list maps the submitted position to a different object. Without an id, the current model object must also be equals() to one of the choices for the option to show as selected. The choices can be a List or a model of a list, as above. A LoadableDetachableModel loads them once per request and keeps them out of the session.

title: Inject EJBs
text: Inject session beans, JNDI resources and persistence units into Wicket components with @EJB, @Resource and @PersistenceUnit, through WicketStuff's javaee-inject module.
keywords: Enterprise JavaBeans EJB session bean Stateless Stateful JNDI java:global java:module Resource PersistenceUnit EntityManagerFactory Jakarta EE TomEE WildFly GlassFish Payara
body: Use this when your business logic lives in Enterprise JavaBeans on a Jakarta EE server and you want to inject them with @EJB. Wicket components are not managed by the server, so the server ignores these annotations on them. The module wicketstuff-javaee-inject from WicketStuff looks the beans up in JNDI when a component is constructed. If your server supports CDI, as every Jakarta EE server does, you can also inject stateless and singleton session beans with @Inject through wicket-cdi, without an extra module.

title: Add the dependency
text: <dependency> <groupId>org.wicketstuff</groupId> <artifactId>wicketstuff-javaee-inject</artifactId> <version>${wicketstuff.version}</version> </dependency> Wicke
body: <dependency> <groupId>org.wicketstuff</groupId> <artifactId>wicketstuff-javaee-inject</artifactId> <version>${wicketstuff.version}</version> </dependency> WicketStuff releases follow the Wicket version numbers: use the WicketStuff release that matches your Wicket version. The module is maintained by the WicketStuff community, not by the Apache Wicket project, so check that a release exists for your Wicket version.

title: Choose the JNDI names
text: By default the injector looks up @EJB fields under java:comp/env/ followed by the name of the annotation, or the fully qualified class name of the field type wh
body: By default the injector looks up @EJB fields under java:comp/env/ followed by the name of the annotation, or the fully qualified class name of the field type when the name is empty. Most servers bind session beans under the portable global names instead. Pass a naming strategy that builds those names: getComponentInstantiationListeners().add( new JavaEEComponentInjector(this, new ModuleJndiNamingStrategy())); Strategy Looks up StandardJndiNamingStrategy (default) java:comp/env/<name or class name> ModuleJndiNamingStrategy java:module/<name or class name> AppJndiNamingStrategy(moduleName) java:app/<module>/<name or class name> GlobalJndiNamingStrategy(moduleName) or (appName, moduleName) java:global/[<app>/]<module>/<class name>, or <name>!<class name> when a name is given The strategies are in package org.wicketstuff.javaee.naming and its subpackage global. Your server logs the JNDI names of each session bean when it deploys the application; pick the strategy that matches them.

title: Inject a session bean
text: OrderService.java @Stateless public class OrderService { public List<Order> openOrders() { /* ... */ } } OrdersPage.java public class OrdersPage extends WebPage
apis: Stateless OrderService List Order OrdersPage WebPage ListView Override ListItem Label Resource DataSource PersistenceUnit EntityManagerFactory Persistence
body: OrderService.java @Stateless public class OrderService { public List<Order> openOrders() { /* ... */ } } OrdersPage.java public class OrdersPage extends WebPage { @EJB private OrderService orders; public OrdersPage() { add(new ListView<Order>("orders", () -> orders.openOrders()) { @Override protected void populateItem(ListItem<Order> item) { item.add(new Label("number", item.getModel().map(Order::getNumber))); } }); } } The field holds a serializable proxy, not the bean, so the page can be stored between requests. The proxy looks the bean up again after deserialization. The module also handles two other annotations: Annotation Injects @EJB A session bean, looked up in JNDI. @Resource(name = "...") Any object bound in JNDI under java:comp/env/ plus that name, such as a DataSource. @PersistenceUnit(unitName = "...") An EntityManagerFactory for the persistence unit, created with Persistence.createEntityManagerFactory().

title: Register the injector
text: WicketApplication.java @Override protected void init() { super.init(); getComponentInstantiationListeners().add(new JavaEEComponentInjector(this)); }
body: WicketApplication.java @Override protected void init() { super.init(); getComponentInstantiationListeners().add(new JavaEEComponentInjector(this)); }

title: Stateful session beans
text: A stateful session bean belongs to one user. The injector keeps one instance per HTTP session for fields whose type is annotated with @Stateful, or whose @EJB a
body: A stateful session bean belongs to one user. The injector keeps one instance per HTTP session for fields whose type is annotated with @Stateful, or whose @EJB annotation has description = "stateful".

title: Link to another site
text: Render a link to a URL outside your application with ExternalLink, build the URL from a model, and redirect to another site from code.
keywords: external URL absolute URL href from model outbound link target blank noopener redirect to external site context relative
body: A link to a fixed address on another site needs no component: write the <a href="https://..."> in the markup. Use an ExternalLink when the address, or the text of the link, depends on data.

title: Link to a file in your web application
text: ExternalLink also links to paths of your own web application that Wicket does not serve, such as a PDF under the webapp root. Call setContextRelative(true), and
body: ExternalLink also links to paths of your own web application that Wicket does not serve, such as a PDF under the webapp root. Call setContextRelative(true), and Wicket makes the path relative to the context root, wherever the current page is: add(new ExternalLink("manual", "/docs/manual.pdf").setContextRelative(true));

title: Open the link in a new tab
text: Put the attributes in the markup, where they belong to the design: Search rel="noreferrer" a
body: Put the attributes in the markup, where they belong to the design: Search rel="noreferrer" also keeps the browser from sending the URL of your page, including a session id in the URL, to the other site. To set attributes from code instead, use an AttributeModifier; see Change a tag’s attributes.

title: Redirect to another site from code
text: When the decision is made on the server, for example after a form submit, throw a RedirectToUrlException. Wicket stops processing the request and sends a redire
body: When the decision is made on the server, for example after a form submit, throw a RedirectToUrlException. Wicket stops processing the request and sends a redirect to the URL: @Override protected void onSubmit() { String url = paymentProvider.startPayment(order); throw new RedirectToUrlException(url); }

title: Render a link with a computed URL
text: Give the anchor a wicket:id: PersonPage.html Search for this person Create the ExternalLink with the URL as a string or as a model. A
apis: Search ExternalLink IModel String URLEncoder StandardCharsets
body: Give the anchor a wicket:id: PersonPage.html Search for this person Create the ExternalLink with the URL as a string or as a model. A model is evaluated each time the page renders, so the link follows changes in the data: PersonPage.java IModel searchUrl = personModel.map(person -> "https://www.example.org/search?q=" + URLEncoder.encode(person.getFullName(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8)); add(new ExternalLink("search", searchUrl)); Wicket writes the URL into the href as it is. Encode values that you put in a query string yourself, as above with URLEncoder. When the model returns null, Wicket does not write an href.

title: Set the text of the link
text: The markup between the tags is the default text. Pass a third argument to replace it: a string when the URL is a string, a model when the URL is a model. add(ne
body: The markup between the tags is the default text. Pass a third argument to replace it: a string when the URL is a string, a model when the URL is a model. add(new ExternalLink("search", searchUrl, personModel.map(person -> "Search for " + person.getFullName()))); The text is escaped before it is written.

title: Update a page with Ajax
text: Make the click counter and the guestbook form update only the parts of the page that change, open the form without a reload, and refresh the guestbook every ten seconds.
keywords: Ajax partial page update no reload setOutputMarkupId setOutputMarkupPlaceholderTag placeholder markup id refresh component show hidden component onConfigure polling timer asynchronous
body: In this tutorial you make the application update parts of a page without reloading it. The click counter on the home page and the guestbook form send their requests in the background, the form opens when a visitor asks for it, and the guestbook refreshes its list by itself. You write no JavaScript: you tell Wicket in Java which components to redraw. Start from the myapp project as you left it at the end of Build a form that saves data.

title: 1. Count clicks without a reload
text: On the home page, the link that counts clicks reloads the page on every click. Replace it with an AjaxLink. Its onClick method gets an AjaxRequestTarget: the li
apis: AjaxLink AjaxRequestTarget Label Void Override Start
body: On the home page, the link that counts clicks reloads the page on every click. Replace it with an AjaxLink. Its onClick method gets an AjaxRequestTarget: the list of components to send back to the browser. In HomePage.java, replace the count link and the clicks label with: Label clicksLabel = new Label("clicks", () -> clicks); clicksLabel.setOutputMarkupId(true); add(clicksLabel); add(new AjaxLink<Void>("count") { @Override public void onClick(AjaxRequestTarget target) { clicks++; target.add(clicksLabel); } }); Import org.apache.wicket.ajax.AjaxRequestTarget and org.apache.wicket.ajax.markup.html.AjaxLink. The HTML stays as it is. setOutputMarkupId(true) makes Wicket write an id attribute on the label’s tag. Wicket’s JavaScript needs that id to find the tag it replaces, so every component you add to the target needs it. Run Start, open the home page and click the link. The number goes up, the rest of the page stays still, and the address in the browser does not change.

title: 2. Give the guestbook list a container
text: You cannot redraw a ListView on its own: it has no tag of its own, only the repeated tags of its items. Wrap it in a WebMarkupContainer, a component that render
apis: ListView WebMarkupContainer Entry Override ListItem Label Ann Hello
body:
You cannot redraw a ListView on its own: it has no tag of its own, only the repeated tags of its items. Wrap it in a WebMarkupContainer, a component that renders its tag and its children and nothing else. In GuestbookPage.java, create the container, and add the ListView to it instead of to the page: WebMarkupContainer entriesContainer = new WebMarkupContainer("entries"); entriesContainer.setOutputMarkupId(true); add(entriesContainer); entriesContainer.add(new ListView("entry", entries) { @Override protected void populateItem(ListItem item) { item.add(new Label("name", item.getModel().map(Entry::getName))); item.add(new Label("text", item.getModel().map(Entry::getText))); } }); Import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.WebMarkupContainer. In GuestbookPage.html, give the
    the container’s id:
    • Ann: Hello!
    Restart and open the guestbook. It looks the same as before.

title: 3. Submit the form with Ajax
text: Replace the plain submit button with an AjaxButton. The form’s onSubmit() still saves the entry; the button’s onSubmit only says what to redraw: the list, the e
body:
Replace the plain submit button with an AjaxButton. The form’s onSubmit() still saves the entry; the button’s onSubmit only says what to redraw: the list, the emptied form and the feedback panel with the thank-you message. In GuestbookPage.java, replace add(new FeedbackPanel("feedback")) so you keep a reference to the panel, give the form and the panel a markup id, and add the button to the form: FeedbackPanel feedback = new FeedbackPanel("feedback"); feedback.setOutputMarkupId(true); add(feedback); form.setOutputMarkupId(true); form.add(new AjaxButton("save") { @Override protected void onSubmit(AjaxRequestTarget target) { target.add(entriesContainer, getForm(), feedback); } }); This code needs entriesContainer, so place it after the container is created. Import org.apache.wicket.ajax.markup.html.form.AjaxButton. In GuestbookPage.html, give the button a wicket:id:

Restart and sign the guestbook. Your entry appears in the list, the form empties and the thank-you message shows, all without a reload. Now submit the form with both fields empty. Nothing happens. The input fails validation, so Wicket does not call onSubmit, and no component is redrawn.

title: 4. Show validation errors
text: When validation fails, an AjaxButton calls its onError method instead. Redraw the feedback panel there. Add this method to the button, next to onSubmit: @Overri
body: When validation fails, an AjaxButton calls its onError method instead. Redraw the feedback panel there. Add this method to the button, next to onSubmit: @Override protected void onError(AjaxRequestTarget target) { target.add(feedback); } Restart and submit the empty form again. The two error messages appear above the form, without a reload.

title: 5. Open the form on request
text: The form takes up the top of the page, above the entries most visitors come to read. Hide it until the visitor asks for it, behind a link that disappears once t
apis: GuestbookPage Form Void Override AjaxLink AjaxRequestTarget Write
body:
The form takes up the top of the page, above the entries most visitors come to read. Hide it until the visitor asks for it, behind a link that disappears once the form is open. A component that is not visible renders nothing, not even its tag. When it becomes visible in an Ajax request, Wicket’s JavaScript then has no tag to replace. setOutputMarkupPlaceholderTag(true) solves this: while the component is hidden, Wicket renders an empty placeholder tag with the component’s id in its place. Add a field to GuestbookPage that remembers whether the visitor opened the form: private boolean writing; Wicket calls onConfigure() on a component each time before it renders it, which makes it the place to decide visibility. Override it in the form, next to onSubmit(): Form form = new Form<>("form") { @Override protected void onConfigure() { super.onConfigure(); setVisible(writing); } @Override protected void onSubmit() { // unchanged } }; Replace form.setOutputMarkupId(true); with: form.setOutputMarkupPlaceholderTag(true); Then add the link, after the form. It opens the form, redraws the form and itself, and hides itself once the form is open: AjaxLink write = new AjaxLink<>("write") { @Override public void onClick(AjaxRequestTarget target) { writing = true; target.add(form, this); } @Override protected void onConfigure() { super.onConfigure(); setVisible(!writing); } }; write.setOutputMarkupPlaceholderTag(true); add(write); Import org.apache.wicket.ajax.markup.html.AjaxLink. In GuestbookPage.html, add the link above the form:

Write a message

Restart and open the guestbook. The page shows the link and the entries. Click the link: the form appears where the placeholder was and the link disappears, without a reload. The form stays open after you sign, ready for the next message.

title: 6. Refresh the list every ten seconds
text: Other visitors sign the guestbook too. A behavior adds functionality to a component without changing its class. AjaxSelfUpdatingTimerBehavior redraws its compon
body: Other visitors sign the guestbook too. A behavior adds functionality to a component without changing its class. AjaxSelfUpdatingTimerBehavior redraws its component at a fixed interval. Add one to the container, after you create it: entriesContainer.add(new AjaxSelfUpdatingTimerBehavior(Duration.ofSeconds(10))); Import org.apache.wicket.ajax.AjaxSelfUpdatingTimerBehavior and java.time.Duration. Restart and open the guestbook in two browsers, or in a normal and a private window, so each has its own session. Sign the guestbook in one. Within ten seconds the new entry appears in the other. Your application now updates parts of its pages over Ajax: from a link, from a form, and on a timer, and it shows a hidden component without a reload.

title: Continue with tests
text: In the next tutorial, Test a page with WicketTester, you write tests for the pages, the form and the Ajax link, and run them without a browser or server. How Wi
body: In the next tutorial, Test a page with WicketTester, you write tests for the pages, the form and the Ajax link, and run them without a browser or server. How Wicket Ajax works explains what happens between the click and the update, Update components with Ajax covers more of AjaxRequestTarget, Show, hide or disable a component explains why visibility belongs in onConfigure(), and Ajax components and Ajax behaviors list what Wicket ships.

title: Build your first application
text: Generate a project from the quickstart, run it, and build a home page with a label, a click counter and a link to a second page.
keywords: hello world getting started quickstart archetype wicket:id first page Jetty Start class setResponsePage
body: In this tutorial you create a Wicket application and write its home page: a greeting, the time on the server, a link that counts your clicks, and a link to a second page. The tutorials after this one continue with the same application. You need a JDK (Java 17 or newer), Apache Maven, and an IDE that opens Maven projects.

title: 1. Generate the project
text: Open a terminal in the folder where you keep your projects and run the quickstart archetype: mvn archetype:generate \ -DarchetypeGroupId=org.apache.wicket \ -Da

body: Open a terminal in the folder where you keep your projects and run the quickstart archetype: mvn archetype:generate \ -DarchetypeGroupId=org.apache.wicket \ -DarchetypeArtifactId=wicket-archetype-quickstart \ -DarchetypeVersion=10.12.0 \ -DgroupId=com.example \ -DartifactId=myapp \ -DinteractiveMode=false To build on Wicket 10, use -DarchetypeVersion=10.12.0 instead. The quickstart page on this site builds the same command for you. Maven creates a folder myapp. These are the files you work with: myapp ├── pom.xml └── src ├── main │ ├── java/com/example │ │ ├── HomePage.html │ │ ├── HomePage.java │ │ └── WicketApplication.java │ └── webapp │ ├── WEB-INF/web.xml │ ├── logo.png │ └── style.css └── test └── java/com/example ├── Start.java └── TestHomePage.java

title: 2. Run the application
text: Open the myapp folder in your IDE as a Maven project. Then run the class Start in src/test/java/com/example: it has a main method that starts an embedded Jetty
body: Open the myapp folder in your IDE as a Maven project. Then run the class Start in src/test/java/com/example: it has a main method that starts an embedded Jetty server with your application. Open http://localhost:8080 in your browser. You see a page that starts with “Congratulations!”. The console shows a warning that Wicket runs in development mode, which is what you want while you build the application. Leave the server running. After each change to a Java file in the steps below, stop Start, run it again and reload the page.

title: 3. Find the three parts of the page
text: The home page you just saw comes from three files. WicketApplication.java is the application class. Its getHomePage() method tells Wicket which page to show at
apis: WicketApplication WebApplication Override Class WebPage HomePage WicketFilter Label
body: The home page you just saw comes from three files. WicketApplication.java is the application class. Its getHomePage() method tells Wicket which page to show at the root URL, and its init() method is where you configure the application: public class WicketApplication extends WebApplication { @Override public Class<? extends WebPage> getHomePage() { return HomePage.class; } @Override public void init() { super.init(); // configuration goes here } } The file WEB-INF/web.xml registers Wicket’s servlet filter, WicketFilter, and passes it the name of this class. HomePage.java and HomePage.html are the page. A page is a Java class with an HTML file of the same name in the same package. Look for wicket:id="version" in the HTML and for new Label("version", ...) in the Java class: the wicket:id attribute ties the tag to the component with the same id.

title: 4. Write your own home page
text: Replace the content of HomePage.java: package com.example; import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.WebPage; import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.basic.Label; publi
apis: WebPage Label HomePage Hello Wicket My App Greeting Start
body:
Replace the content of HomePage.java: package com.example; import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.WebPage; import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.basic.Label; public class HomePage extends WebPage { public HomePage() { add(new Label("greeting", "Hello, Wicket!")); } } And replace HomePage.html: My App

Greeting goes here

Restart Start and reload the page. It shows “Hello, Wicket!” in a heading. The Label component replaced the text between the

tags with its own text. The placeholder text is only there for when you open the HTML file directly in a browser or an editor. Try a typo: change the wicket:id in the HTML to greting and reload. Wicket shows an error page saying that it cannot find a component for that id. Change it back.

title: 5. Show a value that changes
text: A label can also take a lambda instead of a fixed text. Wicket calls the lambda every time it renders the page. Add a label with the time on the server to the c
body:
A label can also take a lambda instead of a fixed text. Wicket calls the lambda every time it renders the page. Add a label with the time on the server to the constructor of HomePage.java: add(new Label("time", () -> LocalTime.now().format(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HH:mm:ss")))); Import java.time.LocalTime and java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter. Add the tag for it to HomePage.html, below the heading:

The time on the server is 12:00:00.

Restart and reload a few times. The time changes on every reload. The lambda is a model: the object a component asks for its value.

title: 6. Count clicks with a link
text: A Wicket Link does not point to a file. It calls its onClick() method on the server when you click it, and then Wicket renders the page again. Add a field and t
apis: Link HomePage WebPage Label Hello Wicket LocalTime DateTimeFormatter Void Override Click You
body:
A Wicket Link does not point to a file. It calls its onClick() method on the server when you click it, and then Wicket renders the page again. Add a field and two components to HomePage.java: public class HomePage extends WebPage { private int clicks; public HomePage() { add(new Label("greeting", "Hello, Wicket!")); add(new Label("time", () -> LocalTime.now().format(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HH:mm:ss")))); add(new Link("count") { @Override public void onClick() { clicks++; } }); add(new Label("clicks", () -> clicks)); } } Import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.link.Link. In HomePage.html, add:

Click me. You clicked 0 times.

Restart, reload and click the link a few times. The number goes up. The field clicks keeps its value between requests because Wicket keeps the page object for you, and the address in the browser now has a number after the question mark that identifies that page object.

title: 7. Add a second page
text: Create AboutPage.java next to HomePage: package com.example; import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.WebPage; import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.link.Link; publi
apis: HomePage WebPage Link AboutPage Void Override About It Apache Wicket Back
body:
Create AboutPage.java next to HomePage: package com.example; import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.WebPage; import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.link.Link; public class AboutPage extends WebPage { public AboutPage() { add(new Link("home") { @Override public void onClick() { setResponsePage(HomePage.class); } }); } } Create AboutPage.html in the same package: About

About this application

It was built with Apache Wicket.

Back to the home page

setResponsePage(HomePage.class) tells Wicket which page to show after the click. Add a link to the new page in the constructor of HomePage: add(new Link("about") { @Override public void onClick() { setResponsePage(AboutPage.class); } }); And in HomePage.html:

About this application

Restart and reload. Click through to the about page and back. The counter on the home page starts at zero again, because setResponsePage(HomePage.class) creates a new HomePage object. You now have an application with two pages, a component that shows a computed value and a link that changes the state of its page.

title: Continue with a shared layout
text: Both pages repeat the same <head> and the same frame around their content. In the next tutorial, Give every page the same layout, you move that into one base pa
body: Both pages repeat the same <head> and the same frame around their content. In the next tutorial, Give every page the same layout, you move that into one base page. To understand what you built: Why component-oriented explains the idea behind pages and components, What models are for explains the lambda you gave the labels, and Stateful and stateless pages explains why the counter keeps its value. Before you put the application on a server, switch it to deployment mode.

title: Build a form that saves data
text: Add a guestbook page with a form that validates its input, saves entries and lists them, and shows errors and a confirmation.
keywords: guestbook form submit onSubmit input required field validation error message feedback wicket:for ListView data entry
apis: Form TextField TextArea LambdaModel ListView FeedbackPanel StringValidator BasePage HeaderPanel FooterPanel
body: In this tutorial you add a guestbook to the application: a page where visitors leave their name and a message, and see the messages others left. You build a form that writes its input into a Java object, check that input, and show errors and a confirmation. Start from the myapp project as you left it at the end of Give every page the same layout, with BasePage, HeaderPanel and FooterPanel in the package com.example.

page: Build a form that saves data
title: 1. Store guestbook entries
text: Create Entry.java for one message in the guestbook. It is serializable because the page that edits it is kept between requests: package com.example; import java
apis: Serializable Entry String List CopyOnWriteArrayList Guestbook Wicket Welcome WicketApplication WebApplication Application Start
body: Create Entry.java for one message in the guestbook. It is serializable because the page that edits it is kept between requests: package com.example; import java.io.Serializable; public class Entry implements Serializable { private String name; private String text; public Entry() { } public Entry(String name, String text) { this.name = name; this.text = text; } public String getName() { return name; } public void setName(String name) { this.name = name; } public String getText() { return text; } public void setText(String text) { this.text = text; } } Create Guestbook.java. It keeps the entries in memory, newest first, and starts with one entry so the page has something to show: package com.example; import java.util.List; import java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList; public class Guestbook { private final List<Entry> entries = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>(); public Guestbook() { entries.add(new Entry("Wicket", "Welcome to the guestbook!")); } public void add(Entry entry) { entries.add(0, entry); } public List<Entry> getEntries() { return List.copyOf(entries); } } The application holds the one guestbook that all visitors share. In WicketApplication.java, add a field, a getter and a static get() method that returns the running application with its own type: public class WicketApplication extends WebApplication { private final Guestbook guestbook = new Guestbook(); public static WicketApplication get() { return (WicketApplication) Application.get(); } public Guestbook getGuestbook() { return guestbook; } // getHomePage() and init() stay as they are } Import org.apache.wicket.Application. Run Start: the application starts and looks as before.

page: Build a form that saves data
title: 2. List the entries on a guestbook page
text: Create GuestbookPage.java: package com.example; import java.util.List; import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.basic.Label; import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.li
apis: List Label ListItem ListView IModel GuestbookPage BasePage Entry WicketApplication Override String Guestbook My App Ann Hello BookmarkablePageLink Void
body:
Create GuestbookPage.java: package com.example; import java.util.List; import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.basic.Label; import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.list.ListItem; import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.list.ListView; import org.apache.wicket.model.IModel; public class GuestbookPage extends BasePage { public GuestbookPage() { IModel> entries = () -> WicketApplication.get().getGuestbook().getEntries(); add(new ListView("entry", entries) { @Override protected void populateItem(ListItem item) { item.add(new Label("name", item.getModel().map(Entry::getName))); item.add(new Label("text", item.getModel().map(Entry::getText))); } }); } @Override protected String getPageTitle() { return "Guestbook - My App"; } } A ListView repeats its tag once for every element of the list in its model, and calls populateItem to fill in each copy. item.getModel() is a model of one entry, and map turns it into a model of one of its properties. Create GuestbookPage.html:

Guestbook

  • Ann: Hello!
Link to the page from the navigation. In HeaderPanel.java, add: add(new BookmarkablePageLink("guestbook", GuestbookPage.class)); And in HeaderPanel.html, inside the
: Guestbook Restart and click “Guestbook” in the header. The page lists the welcome entry.

title: 3. Add a form that saves an entry
text: The form edits a new Entry that the page keeps in a model. Each field gets a LambdaModel that reads and writes one property of that entry. Add the field and the
apis: Entry LambdaModel GuestbookPage BasePage IModel Model Form Void Override WicketApplication TextField String TextArea ListView Name Message Sign
body:
The form edits a new Entry that the page keeps in a model. Each field gets a LambdaModel that reads and writes one property of that entry. Add the field and the form to GuestbookPage.java: public class GuestbookPage extends BasePage { private final IModel entry = Model.of(new Entry()); public GuestbookPage() { Form form = new Form<>("form") { @Override protected void onSubmit() { WicketApplication.get().getGuestbook().add(entry.getObject()); entry.setObject(new Entry()); } }; add(form); TextField name = new TextField<>("name", LambdaModel.of(entry, Entry::getName, Entry::setName)); form.add(name); TextArea text = new TextArea<>("text", LambdaModel.of(entry, Entry::getText, Entry::setText)); form.add(text); // the ListView from step 2 stays here } } The new imports are org.apache.wicket.markup.html.form.Form, TextField and TextArea from the same package, org.apache.wicket.model.Model and org.apache.wicket.model.LambdaModel. Add the form to GuestbookPage.html, between the heading and the list:

title: 4. Check the input
text: Submit the form with both fields empty. An empty entry appears in the list. Make both fields required, give them a name to use in messages, and limit their leng
apis: TextField String LambdaModel Entry Model Name StringValidator TextArea Message FeedbackPanel
body:
Submit the form with both fields empty. An empty entry appears in the list. Make both fields required, give them a name to use in messages, and limit their length. Replace the code that creates the two fields: TextField name = new TextField<>("name", LambdaModel.of(entry, Entry::getName, Entry::setName)); name.setRequired(true); name.setLabel(Model.of("Name")); name.add(StringValidator.maximumLength(50)); form.add(name); TextArea text = new TextArea<>("text", LambdaModel.of(entry, Entry::getText, Entry::setText)); text.setRequired(true); text.setLabel(Model.of("Message")); text.add(StringValidator.maximumLength(500)); form.add(text); Import org.apache.wicket.validation.validator.StringValidator. When a check fails, Wicket does not update the model and does not call onSubmit(). It keeps what the user typed and records an error message instead. To show those messages, add a FeedbackPanel to the constructor: add(new FeedbackPanel("feedback")); Import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.panel.FeedbackPanel, and put its tag above the form in GuestbookPage.html:
Restart and submit the empty form. Nothing is saved, and the page shows: 'Name' is required. 'Message' is required.

title: 5. Confirm a saved entry
text: The feedback panel also shows messages you add yourself. In onSubmit(), add an info message before you replace the entry: @Override protected void onSubmit() {
body: The feedback panel also shows messages you add yourself. In onSubmit(), add an info message before you replace the entry: @Override protected void onSubmit() { Entry saved = entry.getObject(); WicketApplication.get().getGuestbook().add(saved); info("Thanks for signing, " + saved.getName() + "!"); entry.setObject(new Entry()); } The panel marks each message with a CSS class for its level. Add colors for errors and info messages to style.css: .feedbackPanelERROR { color: #c00; } .feedbackPanelINFO { color: #070; } Restart and sign the guestbook. The page thanks you by name in green and lists your entry. An empty submit shows the errors in red. You now have a page that takes input, checks it, saves it in a Java object and shows the result.
