title: Check the credentials in the session
text: Extend AuthenticatedWebSession. Wicket calls authenticate when the user signs in; return true when the username and password are valid. getRoles returns what th
apis: AuthenticatedWebSession AppSession String Request Override Roles
body: Extend AuthenticatedWebSession. Wicket calls authenticate when the user signs in; return true when the username and password are valid. getRoles returns what the user may do, and is what restricted pages are checked against. AppSession.java public class AppSession extends AuthenticatedWebSession { private String username; public AppSession(Request request) { super(request); } @Override protected boolean authenticate(String username, String password) { // check against your own user store, never against a plain-text password if (userStore().verify(username, password)) { this.username = username; return true; } return false; } @Override public Roles getRoles() { return isSignedIn() ? new Roles(Roles.USER) : new Roles(); } public String getUsername() { return username; } } The session class needs a public constructor that takes a Request. When authenticate succeeds, signIn gives the session a new id and binds it, so a session id planted before the sign-in is useless afterwards.

title: Configure the application
text: Extend AuthenticatedWebApplication and name the session class and the sign-in page. WicketApplication.java public class WicketApplication extends AuthenticatedW
apis: AuthenticatedWebApplication WicketApplication Override Class Page HomePage AbstractAuthenticatedWebSession AppSession WebPage SignInPage
body: Extend AuthenticatedWebApplication and name the session class and the sign-in page. WicketApplication.java public class WicketApplication extends AuthenticatedWebApplication { @Override public Class<? extends Page> getHomePage() { return HomePage.class; } @Override protected Class<? extends AbstractAuthenticatedWebSession> getWebSessionClass() { return AppSession.class; } @Override protected Class<? extends WebPage> getSignInPageClass() { return SignInPage.class; } @Override protected void init() { super.init(); // your own configuration } } Always call super.init(): that is where the application installs its authorization strategy.

title: Require a signed-in user on a page
text: Annotate the page, or a base class of all protected pages, with the role every signed-in user has: AccountPage.java @AuthorizeInstantiation(Roles.USER) public c
body: Annotate the page, or a base class of all protected pages, with the role every signed-in user has: AccountPage.java @AuthorizeInstantiation(Roles.USER) public class AccountPage extends WebPage { } When an anonymous user requests the page, the application remembers the requested URL and redirects to the sign-in page. A user who is signed in but lacks the role gets the access-denied page instead. Restrict access by role covers roles, actions and whole packages.

title: Send the user to another page first
text: The redirect to the sign-in page is an intercept: Wicket stores the requested URL, shows another page, and returns to the URL when that page calls continueToOri
body: The redirect to the sign-in page is an intercept: Wicket stores the requested URL, shows another page, and returns to the URL when that page calls continueToOriginalDestination(). You can use the same mechanism for other pages, such as accepting new terms of use, with redirectToInterceptPage(page) on any component or by throwing RestartResponseAtInterceptPageException. Both end the current request handling, so code after them does not run.

title: Sign the user out
text: signOut() marks the user as signed out and invalidates the session at the end of the request. add(new Link<Void>("signOut") { @Override public void onClick() {
body: signOut() marks the user as signed out and invalidates the session at the end of the request. add(new Link<Void>("signOut") { @Override public void onClick() { AuthenticatedWebSession.get().signOut(); setResponsePage(getApplication().getHomePage()); } }); wicket-auth-roles also has a SignOutPage that invalidates the session when it is rendered.

title: Write your own sign-in form
text: Call signIn on the session and continue to the original destination. continueToOriginalDestination() does not return when there is a remembered URL, so the line
apis: SignInPage WebPage String FeedbackPanel StatelessForm Void Override AuthenticatedWebSession Unknown RequiredTextField LambdaModel PasswordTextField
body: Call signIn on the session and continue to the original destination. continueToOriginalDestination() does not return when there is a remembered URL, so the line after it only runs when there was none. SignInPage.java public class SignInPage extends WebPage { private String username; private String password; public SignInPage() { add(new FeedbackPanel("feedback")); var form = new StatelessForm<Void>("form") { @Override protected void onSubmit() { if (AuthenticatedWebSession.get().signIn(username, password)) { continueToOriginalDestination(); setResponsePage(getApplication().getHomePage()); } else { error("Unknown username or password."); } } }; form.add(new RequiredTextField<>("username", LambdaModel.of(() -> username, value -> username = value))); form.add(new PasswordTextField("password", LambdaModel.of(() -> password, value -> password = value))); add(form); } } A StatelessForm keeps the sign-in page stateless, so showing it does not create a session. Build a stateless form explains why that matters.

Generated ids do not have that problem, so prefer them unless something outside Wicket needs a known id.

body: Implement IMarkupIdGenerator, a single method interface, and register it in your application’s init(): @Override protected void init() { super.init(); getMarkupSettings().setMarkupIdGenerator((component, createIfDoesNotExist) -> { Object stored = component.getMarkupIdImpl(); if (stored instanceof String id) { return id; } if (stored == null && !createIfDoesNotExist) { return null; } int sequence = stored instanceof Integer number ? number : component.getSession().nextSequenceValue(); component.setMarkupIdImpl(sequence); return "w" + Integer.toString(sequence, 36); }); } The generator must return the same id every time it is asked about the same component, which is why it stores the sequence number on the component with setMarkupIdImpl.

body: The default generator, DefaultMarkupIdGenerator, combines a prefix with a counter kept in the session, written in hexadecimal. In development mode the prefix is the component id, such as total1f, so you can recognise the element. In deployment mode the prefix is id, such as id1f. Do not rely on a generated id in CSS or tests: it changes with the order in which components get their ids.

body: Call setOutputMarkupId(true). Wicket then writes an id that is unique within the page. Label total = new Label("total", totalModel); total.setOutputMarkupId(true); add(total); Components you repaint with Ajax need it as well: the browser finds the element to replace by this id, so it must be in the page before the Ajax request.

Use it to build JavaScript or to point other attributes at the component: TextField<String> search = new TextField<>("search", queryModel); search.setOutputMarkupId(true); add(search); add(new WebMarkupContainer("hint") .add(AttributeModifier.replace("aria-describedby", search::getMarkupId))); Call getMarkupId() once the component is on a page, for instance from onInitialize, onConfigure, a model or renderHead, not in a constructor where the component has no parent yet. For <label> tags there is a shortcut that needs no Java: <label wicket:for="search"> writes the for attribute and turns on the markup id. See wicket:for.

title: Markup inheritance
text: How a page or panel subclass inherits its parent's HTML along with its Java code, how wicket:child and wicket:extend merge the two, and when panels are the better tool.
keywords: layout template base page master page wicket:child wicket:extend site layout inheritance composition MarkupNotFoundException Expected to find wicket:child in base markup
body: In Wicket, a page is a Java class with an HTML file of the same name. When you subclass a page in Java, the subclass inherits fields and methods as usual. Wicket extends that inheritance to the HTML: a subclass can use its parent’s markup, or add its own markup into a slot the parent leaves open. This is markup inheritance, and it is the usual way a Wicket application gives all its pages the same layout.

title: Deep hierarchies, one slot per level
text: Inheritance can go several levels deep: BasePage frames the site, ShopPage extends BasePage adds a shop navigation and its own <wicket:child/>, and ProductPage
apis: BasePage ShopPage ProductPage WebPage Override Component String EmptyPanel
body: Inheritance can go several levels deep: BasePage frames the site, ShopPage extends BasePage adds a shop navigation and its own <wicket:child/>, and ProductPage extends ShopPage fills that. Each level’s <wicket:extend> may contain a new <wicket:child/> for the next level. What a level cannot have is more than one slot. Markup inheritance follows single inheritance: one parent, one <wicket:child>. A layout with several areas that differ per page, say a sidebar and a main column, does not fit into one slot. For those areas, combine inheritance with panels: the base page adds a panel created by a method that subclasses override. public abstract class BasePage extends WebPage { @Override protected void onInitialize() { super.onInitialize(); add(newSidebar("sidebar")); } protected Component newSidebar(String id) { return new EmptyPanel(id); } } The factory method is called from onInitialize, not the constructor. A subclass’s override may use fields that the subclass’s constructor sets, and those are not set yet while the parent’s constructor runs.

title: Extending the parent’s markup
text: Most of the time a subclass needs both: the parent’s layout around it, its own content inside. The parent marks the place for that content with <wicket:child/>.
body:
Most of the time a subclass needs both: the parent’s layout around it, its own content inside. The parent marks the place for that content with . The subclass writes its content inside in its own file: BasePage.html
Example Inc.
ProductPage.html

Product name

 Wicket merges the two when it loads the markup: the content of takes the place of . Everything outside in the subclass’s file is ignored, so the file can be a complete HTML page for previewing. The merge happens once, and the merged result is cached like any other markup. From then on, Wicket sees one markup file for ProductPage. That has consequences on the Java side too. The header component, added in BasePage’s constructor, and the name label, added in ProductPage’s constructor, are both children of the same page. The ids of the two classes share one namespace, and the subclass adds its components with a plain add, without knowing about the parent’s structure. If a subclass adds a component but forgets to write its tag inside , development mode reports that the component failed to render, and the message reminds you of .

title: Inheritance and composition
text: Panels and markup inheritance solve different parts of the same problem. A panel is composition: a self-contained piece of user interface, with its own class an
body: Panels and markup inheritance solve different parts of the same problem. A panel is composition: a self-contained piece of user interface, with its own class and file, that a page places where it wants. Markup inheritance is a template: the parent decides the frame, and subclasses fill it in. A typical application uses both. Header, menu and footer are panels, because they are self-contained and sometimes appear elsewhere too. A base page puts them in place and leaves a <wicket:child/> for the content. Each page extends the base page and writes only its content. The alternative without inheritance, a base page with a placeholder component that every subclass replaces with a content panel, works too, but it forces a panel class and file on every page, where markup inheritance needs only the page’s own file. The cost of inheritance is coupling. A subclass depends on the ids and slots of all its ancestors, and a change in the base page reaches every page. Keep base pages small and stable, and move parts that vary into panels that subclasses can swap.

title: Panels inherit markup too
text: Everything above holds for panels. A panel subclass without a file uses its parent’s markup. A base panel can put <wicket:child/> inside its <wicket:panel>, and
body: Everything above holds for panels. A panel subclass without a file uses its parent’s markup. A base panel can put <wicket:child/> inside its <wicket:panel>, and a subclass then writes its part in <wicket:extend>. This is how a family of similar panels, say several kinds of dashboard widgets with the same title bar, can share their frame. To build a page layout step by step, follow the tutorial Give every page the same layout. The tags are described in Wicket tags and attributes.

title: The head of the page
text: The <head> of the parent’s file is used for the merged page. A subclass contributes to it with a <wicket:head> section next to its <wicket:extend>. Wicket keeps
body: The <head> of the parent’s file is used for the merged page. A subclass contributes to it with a <wicket:head> section next to its <wicket:extend>. Wicket keeps the <wicket:head> sections of every level, so each class in the hierarchy can add its own styles, scripts or <meta> tags. For CSS and JavaScript files, contributing from Java with renderHead is usually the better choice: it works the same for pages and panels, and Wicket can order the resources and handle their dependencies.

title: Where a class finds its markup
text: When Wicket needs the markup of a page or panel, it looks for a file named after the class, in the class’s package. If there is none, it looks for the file of t
body: When Wicket needs the markup of a page or panel, it looks for a file named after the class, in the class’s package. If there is none, it looks for the file of the superclass, then of its superclass, up the hierarchy. The first file it finds is used. So a subclass without an HTML file renders with its parent’s markup, unchanged. That alone is useful when a subclass only changes behavior: it inherits the parent’s components and their tags, and overrides some methods. If no class in the hierarchy has a file, rendering fails with a MarkupNotFoundException. A subclass with its own file, on the other hand, replaces the parent’s markup completely, unless the file says otherwise.

body: Gradle uses the same coordinates, for example implementation "org.apache.wicket:wicket-core:$wicketVersion" and testImplementation "org.apache.wicket:wicket-tester:$wicketVersion". Gradle also copies only src/main/resources by default; add src/main/java to the resources source set, excluding **/*.java, to keep HTML files next to the classes.

title: HTML files next to the Java classes
text: Wicket loads the markup of a page or panel from the classpath, next to its class. Maven only copies files from src/main/resources to the classpath by default, s
body: Wicket loads the markup of a page or panel from the classpath, next to its class. Maven only copies files from src/main/resources to the classpath by default, so a project that keeps HomePage.html next to HomePage.java in src/main/java needs this in its <build> section: <resources> <resource> <directory>src/main/resources</directory> </resource> <resource> <directory>src/main/java</directory> <includes> <include>**</include> </includes> <excludes> <exclude>**/*.java</exclude> </excludes> </resource> </resources> <testResources> <testResource> <directory>src/test/resources</directory> </testResource> <testResource> <directory>src/test/java</directory> <includes> <include>**</include> </includes> <excludes> <exclude>**/*.java</exclude> </excludes> </testResource> </testResources> Without it, the application compiles but fails at run time with a MarkupNotFoundException. The second half does the same for markup in the test sources, such as test pages. The alternative is to keep the HTML files in src/main/resources, in the same package folders as the classes.

title: Measure with Wicket metrics
text: Count requests and time component creation, rendering and model loading with the experimental wicket-metrics module, AspectJ and Dropwizard Metrics.
keywords: monitoring performance profiling timing Dropwizard Codahale AspectJ load-time weaving aop.xml javaagent Graphite JMX MetricRegistry
body: Use this when you want numbers on what your Wicket application does: how many requests it serves, how long components take to construct and render, how often models load. The module wicket-metrics weaves measuring code into Wicket’s classes with AspectJ and collects the results in a Dropwizard Metrics registry. wicket-metrics is experimental: it lives in the wicket-experimental part of the Wicket build and may change or disappear in a later release. It is published with every Wicket release, with the same version number.

title: Add the dependencies
text: <dependency> <groupId>org.apache.wicket.experimental.wicket10</groupId> <artifactId>wicket-metrics</artifactId> <version>${wicket.version}</version> </dependenc
body: <dependency> <groupId>org.apache.wicket.experimental.wicket10</groupId> <artifactId>wicket-metrics</artifactId> <version>${wicket.version}</version> </dependency> <dependency> <groupId>org.aspectj</groupId> <artifactId>aspectjrt</artifactId> <version>${aspectj.version}</version> </dependency> wicket-metrics brings Dropwizard’s metrics-core and metrics-jmx along. AspectJ is licensed under the Eclipse Public License; include its license when you distribute it.

title: Choose the measurements

apis: WicketFilterInitAspect AspectJ WicketFilterRequestCycleAspect ComponentCreateAspect ComponentOnRenderAspect LoadableDetachableModelLoadAspect WicketFilterRequestCycleUrlAspect IRequestHandlerRespondAspect IRequestHandlerDetachAspect ComponentOnInitializeAspect ComponentOnConfigureAspect ComponentOnDetachAspect ComponentSetResponsePageAspect BehaviorCreateAspect IResourceCreateAspect ResourceReferenceCreateAspect WicketTagCreateAspect IPartialPageRequestHandlerAddAspect IPartialPageRequestHandlerAppendJavaScriptAspect IPartialPageRequestHandlerPrependJavaScriptAspect SessionCountListenerAspect SessionCountListener WebListener
body: Create src/main/resources/META-INF/aop.xml. It tells the weaver which Wicket classes to weave and which aspects to apply. WicketFilterInitAspect is required; the others are optional: <!DOCTYPE aspectj PUBLIC "-//AspectJ//DTD//EN" "http://www.eclipse.org/aspectj/dtd/aspectj.dtd"> <aspectj> <weaver options="-nowarn"> <include within="org.apache.wicket..*"/> </weaver> <aspects> <aspect name="org.apache.wicket.metrics.aspects.WicketFilterInitAspect"/> <aspect name="org.apache.wicket.metrics.aspects.request.WicketFilterRequestCycleAspect"/> <aspect name="org.apache.wicket.metrics.aspects.component.ComponentCreateAspect"/> <aspect name="org.apache.wicket.metrics.aspects.component.ComponentOnRenderAspect"/> <aspect name="org.apache.wicket.metrics.aspects.model.LoadableDetachableModelLoadAspect"/> </aspects> </aspectj> The jar contains wicket-metrics.template.xml with every aspect. The aspects are in subpackages of org.apache.wicket.metrics.aspects: Aspect Metric Measures request.WicketFilterRequestCycleAspect core/application/requestCycle Time per request. request.WicketFilterRequestCycleUrlAspect core/application/request/… Time per request, by URL. requesthandler.IRequestHandlerRespondAspect core/requesthandler/respond Time per request handler response. requesthandler.IRequestHandlerDetachAspect core/requesthandler/detach Time per request handler detach. component.ComponentCreateAspect core/component/create Time to construct each component class. component.ComponentOnInitializeAspect core/component/initialize Time spent in onInitialize(). component.ComponentOnConfigureAspect core/component/configure Time spent in onConfigure(). component.ComponentOnRenderAspect core/component/render Time spent in onRender(). component.ComponentOnDetachAspect core/component/detach Calls of onDetach(). component.ComponentSetResponsePageAspect core/component/redirect Calls of setResponsePage(). model.LoadableDetachableModelLoadAspect core/model/loadabledetachablemodel/load Time spent in load(). behavior.BehaviorCreateAspect core/behavior/create Behaviors created. resource.IResourceCreateAspect core/resource/resource/create Resources created. resource.ResourceReferenceCreateAspect core/resource/reference/create Resource references created. markup.WicketTagCreateAspect core/tags/wicket/create Wicket tags created. ajax.IPartialPageRequestHandlerAddAspect core/ajax/add Components added to Ajax responses. ajax.IPartialPageRequestHandlerAppendJavaScriptAspect core/ajax/appendJavaScript Calls of appendJavaScript(). ajax.IPartialPageRequestHandlerPrependJavaScriptAspect core/ajax/prependJavaScript Calls of prependJavaScript(). session.SessionCountListenerAspect core/session/count Live sessions. Each metric name starts with the name of the Wicket filter and, where it measures a class, ends with that class name. The session count also needs the servlet listener org.apache.wicket.metrics.aspects.session.SessionCountListener. It is annotated with @WebListener, so the container finds it, unless your web.xml is metadata-complete="true"; then declare it in web.xml. The count starts at 0 when the server starts, so clear persisted sessions when you restart, or the number is off. wicket-metrics supports one Wicket filter per web application.

body: Publish the registry as JMX MBeans in your application’s init(), then open them in JConsole or VisualVM: @Override protected void init() { super.init(); WicketMetrics.getSettings().startJmxReporter(); } Timers show count, minimum, maximum, mean and percentiles; meters show counts and rates.

apis: WicketMetrics MetricRegistry GraphiteReporter Override Graphite InetSocketAddress TimeUnit
body: WicketMetrics.getMetricRegistry() returns the Dropwizard MetricRegistry, so every Dropwizard reporter works. To send the numbers to Graphite every five seconds, add io.dropwizard.metrics:metrics-graphite in the version that wicket-metrics uses, and start a reporter: private GraphiteReporter reporter; @Override protected void init() { super.init(); var graphite = new Graphite(new InetSocketAddress("graphite.example.com", 2003)); reporter = GraphiteReporter.forRegistry(WicketMetrics.getMetricRegistry()) .prefixedWith("webapps") .convertRatesTo(TimeUnit.SECONDS) .convertDurationsTo(TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS) .build(graphite); reporter.start(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS); } @Override protected void onDestroy() { reporter.stop(); super.onDestroy(); }

title: Start the AspectJ weaver

body: The measurements are added while classes load, by the AspectJ weaver running as a Java agent. Download aspectjweaver.jar in the same version as aspectjrt and add it to the JVM options of your servlet container, for example in Tomcat’s setenv.sh: CATALINA_OPTS="$CATALINA_OPTS -javaagent:/opt/aspectj/aspectjweaver-1.9.x.jar"

title: Show images from an external URL
text: Render img and source tags whose URL comes from a model with ExternalImage and ExternalSource, for images on another server or a CDN.
keywords: external image image URL from model avatar CDN image remote image img src from database srcset picture element img-src
body: Use ExternalImage when your data holds the address of an image, such as an avatar URL or a product photo on a CDN. Wicket writes the URL from the model into the src attribute and does not serve the image itself.

page: Show images from an external URL
title: Allow the image host in the Content Security Policy
text: The default Content Security Policy only allows images from your own origin, img-src 'self', so the browser blocks images from another host. Add the host in ini
body: The default Content Security Policy only allows images from your own origin, img-src 'self', so the browser blocks images from another host. Add the host in init(): getCspSettings().blocking().add(CSPDirective.IMG_SRC, "https://images.example.com"); See Configure the Content Security Policy. When a script on the page reads the image, for example to draw it on a canvas, the server must allow cross-origin access and the tag needs a crossorigin attribute: photo.setCrossOrigin(CrossOrigin.ANONYMOUS). For images that you serve yourself, use Image with a resource reference instead, see Serve files from your Java packages.

page: Show images from an external URL
title: Offer several sizes
text: The third constructor argument is a model of the URLs for srcset. Add descriptors with setXValues and sizes with setSizes: ExternalImage photo = new ExternalIma
body: The third constructor argument is a model of the URLs for srcset. Add descriptors with setXValues and sizes with setSizes: ExternalImage photo = new ExternalImage("photo", "https://images.example.com/p/42-640.jpg", List.of("https://images.example.com/p/42-640.jpg", "https://images.example.com/p/42-1280.jpg")); photo.setXValues("1x", "2x"); add(photo); Inside a Picture, use ExternalSource for the tags and setMedia for the media query: Picture picture = new Picture("banner"); ExternalSource wide = new ExternalSource("wide", List.of("https://images.example.com/banner-wide.jpg")); wide.setMedia("(min-width: 40em)"); picture.add(wide); picture.add(new ExternalImage("fallback", "https://images.example.com/banner.jpg")); add(picture);

body: Pass a model of the URL. Any Serializable value works; Wicket writes its toString(): UserPanel.java public class UserPanel extends GenericPanel { public UserPanel(String id, IModel userModel) { super(id, userModel); IModel avatarUrl = () -> getModelObject().getAvatarUrl(); add(new ExternalImage("avatar", avatarUrl)); } } UserPanel.html The constructor takes an IModel, so declare the lambda with that type; a model of String does not fit. body: Use this when an attribute of a component’s tag depends on Java state: a CSS class for the current status, a title from the model, an aria-expanded that follows a toggle. Wicket changes attributes through behaviors that you add to the component; the markup keeps its static attributes.

title: Add or remove a boolean attribute
text: Attributes such as hidden, open or required have no value. Pass AttributeModifier.VALUELESS_ATTRIBUTE_ADD to write the attribute without a value, or VALUELESS_A
body: Attributes such as hidden, open or required have no value. Pass AttributeModifier.VALUELESS_ATTRIBUTE_ADD to write the attribute without a value, or VALUELESS_ATTRIBUTE_REMOVE to leave it out: details.add(AttributeModifier.replace("open", () -> expanded ? AttributeModifier.VALUELESS_ATTRIBUTE_ADD : AttributeModifier.VALUELESS_ATTRIBUTE_REMOVE));

title: Add or remove CSS classes as a set
text: ClassAttributeModifier gives you the current classes as a set and writes back the set you return. Use it when you need to remove a class from the markup, or add
body: ClassAttributeModifier gives you the current classes as a set and writes back the set you return. Use it when you need to remove a class from the markup, or add several depending on state. When the set ends up empty, the class attribute is removed. status.add(new ClassAttributeModifier() { @Override protected Set<String> update(Set<String> classes) { classes.remove("badge"); if (order.isLate()) { classes.add("badge-late"); } return classes; } }); StyleAttributeModifier does the same for the declarations in a style attribute, as a map from property to value.

title: Append or prepend to an attribute
text: AttributeModifier.append adds the value after the existing one, separated by a space. prepend puts it in front. Both add the attribute if it is missing. status.
body: AttributeModifier.append adds the value after the existing one, separated by a space. prepend puts it in front. Both add the attribute if it is missing. status.add(AttributeModifier.append("class", () -> order.isLate() ? "badge-late" : null)); With the markup above, a late order renders class="badge badge-late". When the model returns null, nothing is appended. For another separator, use new AttributeAppender(attribute, model, separator), for example ";" for a style attribute.

body: Behavior.onAttribute gets the current value and returns the new one. Behavior.onTag gives you the whole ComponentTag. status.add(Behavior.onAttribute("title", current -> current == null ? "Status" : current.toUpperCase())); status.add(Behavior.onTag((component, tag) -> tag.put("aria-live", "polite")));

body: Pass a model instead of a value. Wicket reads the model each time it renders the tag, so the attribute stays current. status.add(AttributeModifier.replace("data-status", () -> order.getStatus().name())); When the model returns null, the attribute keeps the value it has in the markup.

title: Remove an attribute
text: link.add(AttributeModifier.remove("target"));
body: link.add(AttributeModifier.remove("target"));

title: Replace an attribute value
text: AttributeModifier.replace sets the attribute, overwriting a value from the markup. If the attribute is not in the markup, it is added. OrderPanel.html <span wic
body: AttributeModifier.replace sets the attribute, overwriting a value from the markup. If the attribute is not in the markup, it is added. OrderPanel.html Status OrderPanel.java Label status = new Label("status", order.getStatus()); status.add(AttributeModifier.replace("title", "Order status")); add(status);

title: Set attributes in your own component
text: In a component class you write yourself, override onComponentTag instead of adding a behavior: public class StatusLabel extends Label { private final IModel<Sta
apis: StatusLabel Label IModel Status String Override ComponentTag
body: In a component class you write yourself, override onComponentTag instead of adding a behavior: public class StatusLabel extends Label { private final IModel<Status> status; public StatusLabel(String id, IModel<Status> status) { super(id, status); this.status = status; } @Override protected void onComponentTag(ComponentTag tag) { super.onComponentTag(tag); tag.put("data-status", status.getObject().name()); } } Wicket escapes attribute values when it writes the tag, so a value with quotes or < cannot break out of the attribute. Attribute changes need a tag: on a component with setRenderBodyOnly(true) they have no effect. For more on behaviors, see Add behavior to a component with a Behavior.

Despite the name, it uses the jakarta.websocket API. wicket-native-websocket-core wicket-devutils Tools for development: DebugBar, InspectorPage and the page, session and component inspectors. They work only in development mode. wicket-core, wicket-extensions wicket-velocity VelocityPanel and resources that render Apache Velocity templates. wicket-core wicket-jmx Exposes the application and its settings as JMX MBeans. wicket-core wicket-objectsizeof-agent InstrumentationObjectSizeOfStrategy, which measures object sizes, for example of pages and sessions, through a Java agent. wicket-core wicket-velocity renders a template as markup without escaping it, and does not escape the values it interpolates either. A Velocity template can call methods on the objects in its context, so only use templates written by developers, never templates built from user input.

title: Give pages readable URLs
text: Mount pages on paths of your choice, put page parameters in path segments with placeholders, and mount a whole package at once.
keywords: mountPage mountPackage clean URLs pretty URLs SEO friendly URL route routing path parameter placeholder wicket/bookmarkable enforce mounts
apis: WebApplication MountedMapper PackageMapper UrlPathPageParametersEncoder IMapperContext DefaultMapperContext ProductPage
body: Without a mount, the URL of a page contains its class name, like /wicket/bookmarkable/com.example.ProductPage?id=42. Mount the pages that users see, bookmark or find through search engines, so that their URLs read like /products/42.

title: Encode all parameters as path segments
text: To put every named parameter in the path as name-value pairs, mount the page with a MountedMapper and an UrlPathPageParametersEncoder: mount(new MountedMapper("
body: To put every named parameter in the path as name-value pairs, mount the page with a MountedMapper and an UrlPathPageParametersEncoder: mount(new MountedMapper("/search", SearchPage.class, new UrlPathPageParametersEncoder())); // q=wicket, page=2 -> /search/q/wicket/page/2 This encoder cannot read parameters from a POST request.

title: Mount a page on a path
text: Call mountPage in the init() method of your application: WicketApplication.java @Override protected void init() { super.init(); mountPage("/products", ProductLi
body: Call mountPage in the init() method of your application: WicketApplication.java @Override protected void init() { super.init(); mountPage("/products", ProductListPage.class); mountPage("/about", AboutPage.class); } From now on, every link to ProductListPage, including BookmarkablePageLink and setResponsePage(ProductListPage.class), uses /products, and a request for /products creates the page. Named page parameters go into the query string: /products?sort=price. The home page from getHomePage() is already available at /; you do not need to mount it.

title: Mount all pages of a package
text: mountPackage mounts every bookmarkable page in the package of the class you pass, using the simple class name as the last segment: mountPackage("/admin", UserAd
body: mountPackage mounts every bookmarkable page in the package of the class you pass, using the simple class name as the last segment: mountPackage("/admin", UserAdminPage.class); // com.example.admin.UserAdminPage -> /admin/UserAdminPage // com.example.admin.AuditLogPage -> /admin/AuditLogPage New pages in the package get a URL without a change to init(). Pages in subpackages are not included.

title: Put parameters in the path
text: Use a placeholder for a path segment that holds the value of a named parameter. ${name} is a required parameter: mountPage("/products/${id}", ProductPage.class)
body: Use a placeholder for a path segment that holds the value of a named parameter. ${name} is a required parameter: mountPage("/products/${id}", ProductPage.class); A link with new PageParameters().add("id", 42) now points to /products/42, and in the page parameters.get("id") reads the value from the path, exactly like a query string parameter. A URL without the segment, /products, does not match this mount. #{name} is an optional parameter. When the parameter is missing, the segment is left out: mountPage("/products/${id}/#{tab}", ProductPage.class); // id=42 -> /products/42 // id=42, tab=reviews -> /products/42/reviews A placeholder fills a whole segment; /products-${id} is not a placeholder. Named parameters without a placeholder still go into the query string. The full syntax is listed in Request mappers.

title: Refuse the class name URLs of mounted pages
text: A mounted page stays reachable through /wicket/bookmarkable/<class name>. To accept only the mounted path, turn on enforced mounts: getSecuritySettings().setEnf
body: A mounted page stays reachable through /wicket/bookmarkable/<class name>. To accept only the mounted path, turn on enforced mounts: getSecuritySettings().setEnforceMounts(true); Wicket then refuses every /wicket/bookmarkable/ URL, also for pages that are not mounted. Mount every page that users reach through a BookmarkablePageLink or setResponsePage(SomePage.class) before you turn this on.

title: Rename the wicket prefix of unmounted URLs
text: The fixed segments in unmounted URLs, wicket, bookmarkable, page and resource, come from the mapper context. Override newMapperContext() in your application to
body: The fixed segments in unmounted URLs, wicket, bookmarkable, page and resource, come from the mapper context. Override newMapperContext() in your application to change them: @Override protected IMapperContext newMapperContext() { return new DefaultMapperContext(this) { @Override public String getNamespace() { return "app"; } @Override public String getBookmarkableIdentifier() { return "view"; } }; } Do not start a mount path with one of these reserved segments. To give a resource a URL, see Give a resource a URL.

title: Why a stateful page gets a number in its URL
text: A mounted page that is stateful shows its page id: /products/42?3. Wicket needs the id to find this instance of the page again when the user clicks a link or re
body: A mounted page that is stateful shows its page id: /products/42?3. Wicket needs the id to find this instance of the page again when the user clicks a link or reloads. A stateless page keeps the clean URL. See Stateful and stateless pages.

title: Give a resource a URL
text: Mount a resource reference on a path of your choice with mountResource, read path and query parameters in the resource, and link to the mounted URL.
keywords: mountResource resource URL fixed URL REST endpoint feed URL robots.txt favicon placeholder path parameter urlFor
body: Mount a resource when its URL matters: a feed that readers subscribe to, a file that another system downloads, an export that users bookmark, or a well-known path such as /robots.txt. Without a mount, the URL of a resource starts with wicket/resource/ and contains a class name.

title: Link to a mounted resource
text: Keep the reference in a constant, so links and the mount use the same instance, and pass parameters with PageParameters: Resources.java public final class Resou
apis: PageParameters Resources ResourceReference InvoicePdfResource ResourceLink Void RequestCycle Component
body: Keep the reference in a constant, so links and the mount use the same instance, and pass parameters with PageParameters: Resources.java public final class Resources { public static final ResourceReference INVOICE = ResourceReference.of("invoice", InvoicePdfResource::new); private Resources() { } } WicketApplication.java mountResource("/invoices/${number}", Resources.INVOICE); InvoicePanel.java add(new ResourceLink<Void>("pdf", Resources.INVOICE, new PageParameters().add("number", invoice.getNumber()))); The link renders /invoices/2024-0042. To get the URL as text, for example for an e-mail, use RequestCycle.get().urlFor(Resources.INVOICE, parameters), or Component#urlFor inside a component. Links to resource references are stateless, so they work on stateless pages.

title: Mount a file from a package
text: A package resource can be mounted too, so that a fixed path answers requests that do not come from your pages. Links that Wicket renders to it add the version t
body: A package resource can be mounted too, so that a fixed path answers requests that do not come from your pages. Links that Wicket renders to it add the version to the file name, as for any package resource; requests without the version still work. mountResource("/robots.txt", new PackageResourceReference(WicketApplication.class, "robots.txt")); mountResource("/favicon.ico", new PackageResourceReference(WicketApplication.class, "favicon.ico")); The package resource guard still applies, so the file type must be one it serves; see Control which package resources are served.

title: Mount a resource reference
text: Call mountResource in init() with the path and a resource reference. ResourceReference.of turns a supplier of the resource into a reference: WicketApplication.j
body: Call mountResource in init() with the path and a resource reference. ResourceReference.of turns a supplier of the resource into a reference: WicketApplication.java @Override protected void init() { super.init(); mountResource("/exports/orders.csv", ResourceReference.of("orders.csv", OrdersCsvResource::new)); } A request for /exports/orders.csv is now answered by the resource, and every link to the reference uses that URL. OrdersCsvResource is the resource from Generate a resource in code. A mounted resource serves all users of the application. Keep no per-user state in it, and check in the resource whether the current user may see the data, because anyone can type the URL. The path must not start with a segment that Wicket reserves for itself, such as wicket.

title: Put parameters in the path
text: A segment written as ${name} is a placeholder. Wicket takes the value from the URL and passes it to the resource as a named parameter: mountResource("/invoices/
apis: ResourceReference InvoicePdfResource Override ResourceResponse Attributes String Invoice InvoiceService WriteCallback IOException
body: A segment written as ${name} is a placeholder. Wicket takes the value from the URL and passes it to the resource as a named parameter: mountResource("/invoices/${number}", ResourceReference.of("invoice", InvoicePdfResource::new)); In the resource, read it from the attributes: InvoicePdfResource.java @Override protected ResourceResponse newResourceResponse(Attributes attributes) { String number = attributes.getParameters().get("number").toString(""); Invoice invoice = InvoiceService.get().findForCurrentUser(number); if (invoice == null) { return new ResourceResponse().setError(404); } byte[] pdf = InvoiceService.get().renderPdf(invoice); ResourceResponse response = new ResourceResponse(); response.setContentType("application/pdf"); response.setFileName("invoice-" + number + ".pdf"); response.setWriteCallback(new WriteCallback() { @Override public void writeData(Attributes attributes) throws IOException { attributes.getResponse().write(pdf); } }); return response; } Segments after the mount path become indexed parameters, and a query string becomes named parameters, as for pages: /invoices/2024-0042?download=true. Pass parameters to a page shows how to read both kinds.

page: Use more than one model in a component
title: Use more than one model in a component
text: Detach the extra models a component, behavior or custom model keeps in its fields, so their data is not stored with the page.
keywords: onDetach detach second model additional model model field detachModels onDetachAlways nested model memory leak page size
body: You need this when a component works with more than one model. A component has one default model, and Wicket detaches that one at the end of each request. Any other model you keep in a field is detached only when you do it yourself. A model that is not detached keeps its loaded object, which is then stored with the page.

page: Use more than one model in a component
title: Detach extra models in onDetach
text: Override onDetach() in the component, detach each model you keep, and call super.onDetach(): PersonOrdersPanel.java public class PersonOrdersPanel extends Gener
apis: PersonOrdersPanel GenericPanel Person IModel List Order String Label ListView Override ListItem
body: Override onDetach() in the component, detach each model you keep, and call super.onDetach(): PersonOrdersPanel.java public class PersonOrdersPanel extends GenericPanel<Person> { private final IModel<List<Order>> orders; public PersonOrdersPanel(String id, IModel<Person> person, IModel<List<Order>> orders) { super(id, person); this.orders = orders; add(new Label("name", person.map(Person::getName))); add(new ListView<>("orders", orders) { @Override protected void populateItem(ListItem<Order> item) { item.add(new Label("number", item.getModel().map(Order::getNumber))); } }); } @Override protected void onDetach() { orders.detach(); super.onDetach(); } } Wicket checks that super.onDetach() is called and fails the request with an error when it is not. Detaching the same model twice does no harm. Here the ListView also detaches orders, because it is the list view’s default model, but the panel cannot rely on that: the list view might be replaced or removed.

page: Use more than one model in a component
title: Detach models held by a behavior
text: A behavior that keeps a model overrides detach(Component): public class TitleBehavior extends Behavior { private final IModel<String> title; public TitleBehavio
apis: Component TitleBehavior Behavior IModel String Override ComponentTag AttributeModifier
body: A behavior that keeps a model overrides detach(Component): public class TitleBehavior extends Behavior { private final IModel<String> title; public TitleBehavior(IModel<String> title) { this.title = title; } @Override public void onComponentTag(Component component, ComponentTag tag) { tag.put("title", title.getObject()); } @Override public void detach(Component component) { title.detach(); super.detach(component); } } AttributeModifier and the other behaviors in Wicket that take a model already detach it.

page: Use more than one model in a component
title: Detach models inside your own model
text: A model that wraps other models detaches them in its own detach(): public class FullNameModel implements IModel<String> { private final IModel<String> first; pr
apis: FullNameModel IModel String Override LambdaModel LoadableDetachableModel OrdersModel List Order SpringBean OrderService Person Injector
body: A model that wraps other models detaches them in its own detach(): public class FullNameModel implements IModel<String> { private final IModel<String> first; private final IModel<String> last; public FullNameModel(IModel<String> first, IModel<String> last) { this.first = first; this.last = last; } @Override public String getObject() { return first.getObject() + " " + last.getObject(); } @Override public void detach() { first.detach(); last.detach(); } } The models made by map, combineWith, LambdaModel.of(target, ...) and the other model methods in Wicket already do this. first.combineWith(last, (f, l) -> f + " " + l) replaces the whole class above. A LoadableDetachableModel that uses other models overrides detach(), calls super.detach() and detaches the other models there, so they are detached also in requests where the model itself was never loaded: public class OrdersModel extends LoadableDetachableModel<List<Order>> { @SpringBean private OrderService orderService; private final IModel<Person> person; public OrdersModel(IModel<Person> person) { this.person = person; Injector.get().inject(this); } @Override protected List<Order> load() { return orderService.findByCustomer(person.getObject()); } @Override public void detach() { super.detach(); person.detach(); } } onDetach() is the wrong place: it only runs when the model itself was loaded in the request. Load data once per request with detachable models covers LoadableDetachableModel itself.

page: Use more than one model in a component
title: Pass derived models instead of fields
text: A model you hand to a child component is detached with that child. When the panel only needs a model to build its children, do not keep it in a field. The perso
body: A model you hand to a child component is detached with that child. When the panel only needs a model to build its children, do not keep it in a field. The person model above is the panel’s default model, and the label gets person.map(...), which detaches person too.

title: Nest forms
text: Put a form inside another form, submit and validate the inner form on its own, and decide which forms take part in a submit.
keywords: nested form inner form subform form in form wantSubmitOnNestedFormSubmit wantSubmitOnParentFormSubmit
body: You need this when part of a form must be submitted and validated on its own, such as an “Add address” section inside a customer form, or when you reuse a panel that contains its own form. HTML does not allow a form inside a form. Wicket does: it renders the outer form as the only <form> and every nested form as a <div>, and keeps track of which form a submit belongs to.

title: Put a form inside another form
text: Add the inner form to a component inside the outer form, and nest the markup the same way. Forms can be nested to any depth. CustomerPage.java Form<Customer> cu
apis: Form Customer Override TextField LambdaModel IModel Address Model Button Add Save
body: Add the inner form to a component inside the outer form, and nest the markup the same way. Forms can be nested to any depth. CustomerPage.java Form<Customer> customerForm = new Form<>("customerForm", customerModel) { @Override protected void onSubmit() { customerService.save(getModelObject()); } }; add(customerForm); customerForm.add(new TextField<>("name", LambdaModel.of(customerModel, Customer::getName, Customer::setName)).setRequired(true)); IModel<Address> newAddress = Model.of(new Address()); Form<Address> addressForm = new Form<>("addressForm", newAddress); customerForm.add(addressForm); addressForm.add(new TextField<>("street", LambdaModel.of(newAddress, Address::getStreet, Address::setStreet)).setRequired(true)); addressForm.add(new Button("addAddress") { @Override public void onSubmit() { customerModel.getObject().addAddress(newAddress.getObject()); newAddress.setObject(new Address()); } }); CustomerPage.html <form wicket:id="customerForm"> <input type="text" wicket:id="name"> <form wicket:id="addressForm"> <input type="text" wicket:id="street"> <button type="submit" wicket:id="addAddress">Add address</button> </form> <button type="submit">Save customer</button> </form>

title: Show the messages of each form
text: A single FeedbackPanel shows the messages of both forms. To show them per form without duplicates, give each form a FencedFeedbackPanel with the form as fence:
body: A single FeedbackPanel shows the messages of both forms. To show them per form without duplicates, give each form a FencedFeedbackPanel with the form as fence: customerForm.add(new FencedFeedbackPanel("customerFeedback", customerForm)); addressForm.add(new FencedFeedbackPanel("addressFeedback", addressForm)); The outer panel then leaves out the messages that come from inside the address form.

title: Submit everything from the outer form
text: A button of the outer form, or a plain submit button, submits the outer form together with all nested forms. Every form is validated; if any field in any of the
body: A button of the outer form, or a plain submit button, submits the outer form together with all nested forms. Every form is validated; if any field in any of them is invalid, no model is updated. When all are valid, onSubmit() is called on the innermost forms first and on the outer form last. To leave a nested form out when its parent is submitted, override wantSubmitOnParentFormSubmit() in the nested form: Form<Address> addressForm = new Form<>("addressForm", newAddress) { @Override protected boolean wantSubmitOnParentFormSubmit() { return false; } }; Without this, the “Save customer” button in the example would fail on an empty street field. With it, the address section is neither validated nor updated when the customer is saved.

title: Submit only the inner form
text: A button inside the inner form submits only that form. Wicket validates the inner form, updates its models and calls its onSubmit(). The outer form is not valid
body: A button inside the inner form submits only that form. Wicket validates the inner form, updates its models and calls its onSubmit(). The outer form is not validated, so “Add address” works while the customer name is still empty. The browser does send the input of the whole page. Wicket shows what the user typed in the outer fields again, but does not validate or store it.

title: Submit the outer form along with the inner form
text: To make a submit of the inner form process the outer form as well, override wantSubmitOnNestedFormSubmit() in the outer form and return true. A submit from the
body: To make a submit of the inner form process the outer form as well, override wantSubmitOnNestedFormSubmit() in the outer form and return true. A submit from the nested form then processes the outermost form that wants it, together with all forms inside it.

title: Serve files with NIO
text: Serve files from the file system or from inside a ZIP archive through java.nio.file.Path with FileSystemResourceReference and FileSystemResource, including byte ranges for media.
keywords: java.nio Path file system serve file from disk zip file jar file uploaded files media streaming range request FileSystemProvider
apis: FileSystemResourceReference FileSystemResource FileSystemPathService FileSystemJarPathService Video Path
body: Use FileSystemResourceReference when the files you serve live outside the web application and the classpath: uploads on a shared disk, generated reports in a folder, or media inside a ZIP archive. It works with any java.nio.file.Path, so the same code serves a file on disk or an entry in an archive.

title: Mount a folder of files
text: Write a reference that builds the path from a parameter, and keep one instance of it: MediaReference.java public class MediaReference extends FileSystemResource
apis: MediaReference FileSystemResourceReference Path Paths Override IResource FileSystemResource ResourceResponse Attributes String
body: Write a reference that builds the path from a parameter, and keep one instance of it: MediaReference.java public class MediaReference extends FileSystemResourceReference { public static final MediaReference INSTANCE = new MediaReference(); private static final Path FOLDER = Paths.get("/srv/example/media"); private MediaReference() { super(MediaReference.class, "media"); } @Override public IResource getResource() { return new FileSystemResource() { @Override protected ResourceResponse newResourceResponse(Attributes attributes) { String name = attributes.getParameters().get("name").toString(""); if (!name.matches("[\\w-]+(\\.[\\w-]+)*")) { return new ResourceResponse().setError(404); } return createResourceResponse(attributes, FOLDER.resolve(name)); } }; } } Mount it with a placeholder for the file name: WicketApplication.java @Override protected void init() { super.init(); mountResource("/media/${name}", MediaReference.INSTANCE); } /media/intro.mp4 now serves /srv/example/media/intro.mp4. The response gets the content type from the file name and supports HTTP range requests, so a video player can seek, and Wicket streams the file instead of loading it into memory. The name comes from the URL. Check it before you use it in a path, as the example does, so that a request cannot reach outside the folder with .. or a slash.

title: Play a file in a page
text: Give a media component the reference and the file name as a parameter: add(new Video("intro", MediaReference.INSTANCE, new PageParameters().add("name", "intro.m
apis: Video MediaReference PageParameters ResourceLink FileSystemResourceReference Path CSPDirective CSPDirectiveSrcValue
body: Give a media component the reference and the file name as a parameter: add(new Video("intro", MediaReference.INSTANCE, new PageParameters().add("name", "intro.mp4"))); <video wicket:id="intro" controls></video> The src becomes /media/intro.mp4. A ResourceLink with the same reference and parameters offers the file as a download. FileSystemResourceReference also has a constructor that takes the path directly, new FileSystemResourceReference("intro", path). That reference keeps the Path in a field, and Path is not serializable, so a stateful page that holds it cannot be stored. Prefer a reference that builds the path while it responds, as above. The default Content Security Policy sets no media-src directive and falls back to default-src 'none', which blocks video and audio. Allow your own origin in init(): getCspSettings().blocking().add(CSPDirective.MEDIA_SRC, CSPDirectiveSrcValue.SELF);

title: Serve an entry from a ZIP archive
text: FileSystemResourceReference.getPath(URI) creates the path for a URI and opens the file system it needs. For a jar: URI it opens the archive as a file system and
body: FileSystemResourceReference.getPath(URI) creates the path for a URI and opens the file system it needs. For a jar: URI it opens the archive as a file system and keeps it open for the application. Replace the last line of newResourceResponse with: try { URI uri = URI.create("jar:file:///srv/example/media/videos.zip!/videos/" + name); return createResourceResponse(attributes, FileSystemResourceReference.getPath(uri)); } catch (IOException | URISyntaxException e) { throw new WicketRuntimeException("Cannot open " + name, e); }

title: Support another file system
text: getPath asks every FileSystemPathService found with java.util.ServiceLoader whether it handles the URI, and falls back to Paths.get(uri). Wicket’s own FileSyste
apis: FileSystemPathService ServiceLoader Paths FileSystemJarPathService Map String FileSystemProvider
body: getPath asks every FileSystemPathService found with java.util.ServiceLoader whether it handles the URI, and falls back to Paths.get(uri). Wicket’s own FileSystemJarPathService handles jar: URIs. To serve from a file system of your own, implement FileSystemPathService with isResponsible(URI) and getPath(URI, Map<String, String>), and list the class in META-INF/services/org.apache.wicket.resource.FileSystemPathService. The file system itself is a standard java.nio.file.spi.FileSystemProvider.

page: Control which package resources are served
title: Control which package resources are served
text: Allow or block files on the classpath that browsers may request as package resources, with patterns on SecurePackageResourceGuard.
keywords: classpath files file extensions pdf mp4 json access denied to shared resource whitelist static files addPattern
body: You need this when a browser gets “access denied” for a file you serve from a Java package, or when you want to make sure a file next to your classes can never be downloaded. Every request for a package resource passes the package resource guard first. The default guard, SecurePackageResourceGuard, refuses everything that is not explicitly allowed.

page: Control which package resources are served
title: Allow more files
text: Add a pattern to the guard in init(): WicketApplication.java @Override protected void init() { super.init(); if (getResourceSettings().getPackageResourceGuard()

When the guard refuses a file, Wicket logs a warning such as “Access denied to shared (static) resource because of the file extension”.

body: getResourceSettings().setPackageResourceGuard(guard) installs your own IPackageResourceGuard. Extend SecurePackageResourceGuard to keep the default rules, or PackageResourceGuard for a guard that applies only the fixed refusals listed above and allows every other file. Serve files from your Java packages shows how to reference package resources from your components.

page: Control which package resources are served
title: Write a pattern
text: Pattern Matches +*.pdf Every PDF file, in any package +com/example/docs/*.pdf PDF files directly in com/example/docs +com/example/*/*.pdf PDF files exactly one
body: Pattern Matches +*.pdf Every PDF file, in any package +com/example/docs/*.pdf PDF files directly in com/example/docs +com/example/*/*.pdf PDF files exactly one level below com/example +com/example/**/*.pdf PDF files in com/example or any package below it +**/public/*.pdf PDF files in any package whose last part is public -**/secret.txt Blocks secret.txt everywhere The rules: A pattern starts with + to allow or - to block. * stands for any characters within one file or directory name, ** for any number of directories. A pattern without a / is matched against the file name only. A pattern with a / is matched against the whole path from the classpath root, such as com/example/docs/manual.pdf. Patterns are checked from the last added to the first, and the first one that matches decides. Add a blocking pattern after the allowing pattern it should override. Avoid patterns like +*.pdf that allow an extension everywhere: any PDF on the classpath, including those in libraries, becomes downloadable. Name the package.

body: In this tutorial you give the application from Build your first application one layout for all its pages: a header with navigation, a footer, and a page title that each page fills in. You build it with a base page that other pages extend, and with panels for the header and the footer. Start from the myapp project as you left it at the end of the previous tutorial, with HomePage and AboutPage in the package com.example.

Create BasePage.java in com.example: package com.example; import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.WebPage; public abstract class BasePage extends WebPage { } Create BasePage.html next to it. It holds everything the pages share, and a tag where each page puts its own content: My App

My App

Now let HomePage extend BasePage instead of WebPage: public class HomePage extends BasePage { A page that extends another page also inherits its markup. The page’s own HTML file then only provides what goes in place of , inside a tag. Replace HomePage.html with:

 Wicket ignores everything outside , so the and tags are only there to keep the file valid HTML for your editor. Run Start and open http://localhost:8080. The home page now has a blue header with the Wicket logo and a footer. The greeting, time and counter work as before.

A panel is a component with its own HTML file, which you can place on any page. Use one for the header, so it can hold links to every page. Create HeaderPanel.java: package com.example; import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.link.BookmarkablePageLink; import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.panel.Panel; public class HeaderPanel extends Panel { public HeaderPanel(String id) { super(id); add(new BookmarkablePageLink("home", HomePage.class)); add(new BookmarkablePageLink("about", AboutPage.class)); } } A BookmarkablePageLink points straight at a page class. Unlike a Link, it needs no onClick(), and its URL works when you bookmark it or open it in a new tab. Create HeaderPanel.html. The markup of a panel goes inside a tag:

My App

Home About
In BasePage.html, replace the content of the header
with a tag for the panel:
Add the panel in a constructor of BasePage: public abstract class BasePage extends WebPage { protected BasePage() { add(new HeaderPanel("header")); } } The navigation replaces the links between the pages, so remove the about link from HomePage and the home link from AboutPage, in both the Java class and the HTML file. AboutPage keeps an empty constructor, or none at all. Make the navigation readable on the blue header by adding these lines to src/main/webapp/style.css: #nav { float: right; padding-top: 20px; } #nav a, #nav a:visited { color: white; margin-left: 1em; } Restart and reload. The header shows “Home” and “About” on every page, and the links take you between them.

body: Every page still has the title “My App” in the browser tab. Make the title a label whose text comes from a method that pages can override. In BasePage.html, give the <title> tag a wicket:id: <title wicket:id="title">My App</title> In BasePage, add the label and the method: public abstract class BasePage extends WebPage { protected BasePage() { add(new Label("title", this::getPageTitle)); add(new HeaderPanel("header")); add(new FooterPanel("footer")); } protected String getPageTitle() { return "My App"; } } Import org.apache.wicket.markup.html.basic.Label. The method reference is a model, like the lambdas in the previous tutorial: Wicket calls getPageTitle() when it renders the title, so an override in a subclass is used. Override the method in AboutPage: public class AboutPage extends BasePage { @Override protected String getPageTitle() { return "About - My App"; } } Restart and open the about page. The browser tab shows “About - My App”, and the home page keeps “My App”. Your application now has one layout. A new page only needs to extend BasePage and put its content in a <wicket:extend> tag.
